93	- `LIKE` operands and `ESCAPE` must be TEXT or NULL. `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` operands and `WHERE`/`ON`/`HAVING` conditions must be INTEGER, REAL or NULL type; nonzero is true, zero is false, NULL is unknown.
94	- Integer `/` truncates toward zero (`-7 / 2` = `-3`); integer `%` takes the sign of the dividend (`-7 % 2` = `-1`, `7 % -2` = `1`). REAL `/` is float division; REAL `%` is `math.fmod`.
95	- If either arithmetic operand is NULL the result is NULL (checked first). Otherwise a zero divisor for `/` or `%` (INTEGER or REAL) raises RuntimeError `division by zero` at the operator.
96	
97	### NULL and predicates
98	
99	- Any comparison with a NULL operand is NULL. `NOT NULL` is NULL. `AND`: false if either side false, else NULL if either NULL, else true. `OR`: true if either true, else NULL if either NULL, else false.
100	- `x IS NULL` / `x IS NOT NULL` return 1/0, never NULL.
101	- `x [NOT] IN (list)`: NULL if `x` is NULL; 1 if some item equals `x`; else NULL if any item is NULL; else 0. `NOT IN` negates with 3VL.
102	- `LIKE`: whole-string, case-sensitive; `%` matches any sequence (including empty), `_` exactly one character. With `ESCAPE 'c'`, `c` followed by `%`, `_` or `c` matches that character literally; `c` followed by anything else or at pattern end raises RuntimeError `invalid LIKE pattern` at the `LIKE` token. `ESCAPE` must be a one-character string literal. Any NULL operand gives NULL.
103	- Equality for `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT` treats NULL as equal to NULL; join conditions follow normal 3VL, so NULL never matches.
104	
105	### Type inference
106	
107	For each column, over its non-empty raw fields (no trimming): if every field fully matches `[+-]?[0-9]+` the column is INTEGER (`int(field)`); else if every field fully matches `[+-]?([0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+|[0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` it is REAL (`float(field)`); else TEXT (fields kept verbatim, including numeric-looking ones). A column with no non-empty fields is TEXT. Empty fields (quoted or not) are NULL in every type. Consequently `" 1"` makes a column TEXT, `007` is INTEGER `7`, and `1`, `2.5` makes a REAL column.
108	
109	## Interface contract
110	
111	### Data directory
112	
113	- `--data DIR` (default `.`); library `connect(DIR)`. A missing or non-directory `DIR` is an IOError: `connect(DIR)` raises `DataIOError` immediately, and the one-shot CLI reports it and exits 3 before lexing the SQL.
114	- A table is any regular file directly in `DIR` whose name ends in `.csv` (case-insensitive). Table name = file stem; lookup is case-insensitive. Two files whose stems are equal case-insensitively make every reference to that name an IOError `ambiguous table file '<name>'`.
115	- Files are read on each `execute` with `encoding='utf-8-sig'`, `newline=''` and `csv.reader(f, strict=True)` (default dialect). Only the tables referenced in `FROM`/`JOIN` are read; any other file in `DIR`, however malformed, never affects a query. `tables()` lists stems without reading file contents.
116	- Row 1 is the header; names are used verbatim. Empty header name, or duplicate names (case-insensitive), is an IOError. Lines yielding zero fields are skipped. A record with a different field count than the header is IOError `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M`, where N is the reader's `line_num` after that record.
117	
118	### Name resolution and output names
119	
120	- Column reference `c` searches all tables in `FROM`; `q.c` searches the table whose range name (alias, else table name) is `q`. Zero matches: unknown column; more than one: ambiguous column. Duplicate range names are a SemanticError. An `ON` condition sees only tables introduced before or in its own join; later tables are unknown there. Joins associate left.
121	- `*` expands to all columns of all tables in `FROM` order; `t.*` to that table's columns. Duplicate output names are allowed.
122	- Output name: the alias as written (quotes removed); else for an unparenthesized column reference, the column's header name as in the CSV; else the verbatim source text of the item from its first to last character (e.g. `COUNT(*)`, `a + 1`, `(a)`).
123	
124	### Aggregates and grouping
125	
126	- A query is an aggregate query if it has `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, or an aggregate call in the select list or `ORDER BY`.
127	- `COUNT(*)` counts rows; `COUNT(e)` counts non-NULL values (INTEGER). `SUM` of INTEGER is INTEGER, of REAL is REAL. `AVG` is REAL. `MIN`/`MAX` keep the argument type. All ignore NULLs. Over zero non-NULL values `COUNT` is `0`, others NULL. `SUM`/`AVG` need numeric arguments; only `COUNT` accepts `*`.
128	- Without `GROUP BY` the whole filtered input (after `WHERE`) forms a single group, even when empty; without `HAVING` the query yields exactly one row, and `HAVING` filters that group, yielding 0 or 1 row (1 row over empty input when `HAVING` is true, e.g. `HAVING COUNT(*) = 0`). With `GROUP BY`, empty input yields zero rows; groups appear in first-seen order unless ordered.
129	- In an aggregate query, every select, `HAVING` and `ORDER BY` expression must be built from aggregate calls, literals, and subexpressions structurally identical to a `GROUP BY` expression (same resolved columns, operators and literals). `*` is not allowed. Aggregates are not allowed in `WHERE`, `ON`, `GROUP BY`, or inside another aggregate.
130	
131	### ORDER BY, DISTINCT, LIMIT
132	
133	- An `ORDER BY` item that is a bare INTEGER literal is a 1-based output ordinal, counted after `*` expansion. A bare identifier equal to exactly one select-item alias (written with or without `AS`) refers to that output column (two such aliases: ambiguous column). Otherwise it is an expression over input rows (or groups).
134	- With `DISTINCT`, each `ORDER BY` item must be an ordinal, an alias, or structurally identical to a select expression.
135	- Sorting is stable; ties keep pre-sort order for both `ASC` and `DESC`. NULL sorts before every value (first in `ASC`, last in `DESC`).
136	- `LIMIT 0` yields no rows; `OFFSET` past the end yields no rows.
137	
138	### Evaluation order
139	
140	1. `FROM`/joins: nested loop; for each left row in order, right rows in file order; `ON` evaluated for every pair; `LEFT JOIN` emits one NULL-filled row for an unmatched left row.
141	2. `WHERE` per row. 3. Group keys and aggregate arguments per surviving row. 4. `HAVING` per group. 5. Select expressions per surviving row/group. 6. `ORDER BY` keys. 7. `DISTINCT` (first occurrence kept). 8. Sort. 9. `OFFSET`, then `LIMIT`.
142	
143	`AND` skips its right side when the left is false; `OR` when the left is true. Rows are processed in order within each step; the first failure is reported and no output is produced.
144	
145	### Library API
146	
147	```python
148	minisql.connect(data_dir: str | os.PathLike) -> Connection
149	Connection.execute(sql: str) -> Result
150	Connection.tables() -> list[str]                    # stems, sorted by (lower(), name)
151	Connection.schema(table: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]  # (column, type) in header order
152	@dataclass(frozen=True)
153	class Result: columns: list[str]; types: list[str]; rows: list[tuple]
154	minisql.format_csv(result: Result) -> str
155	minisql.format_table(result: Result) -> str
156	```
157	
158	`types` holds `"INTEGER"`, `"REAL"`, `"TEXT"` or `"NULL"`. Row values are `int`, `float`, `str` or `None`.
159	
160	### Output formats
161	
162	Value text: INTEGER `str(v)`; REAL `repr(v)` (`100.0`, `2.5`, `1e+20`); TEXT verbatim.
163	
164	**CSV** (`--format csv`, default for one-shot): header line, then one line per row, fields joined by `,`, every line terminated by `\n` (also on Windows). NULL is an empty unquoted field. A field is wrapped in `"` (inner `"` doubled) iff it is the empty string, contains `,`, `"`, `\n` or `\r`, or starts or ends with a space. Header names follow the same quoting.
165	
166	**Table** (`--format table`, default for REPL): cell text is the value text with newline and carriage-return characters replaced by the two-character escapes `\n` and `\r`; NULL is `NULL`. Width of a column = max code-point length of header and cells. Header cells left-aligned; INTEGER/REAL values right-aligned; TEXT and `NULL` left-aligned. Cells joined by ` | `; separator line is `-` × width per column joined by `-+-`; trailing spaces stripped from every line; then `(N rows)` or `(1 row)`. Every line ends with `\n`.
167	
168	### CLI
169	
170	`python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]`. With `SQL`: one-shot, print the formatted result to stdout. Without `SQL`: REPL on stdin. stdout and stderr are UTF-8 with `\n`.
171	
172	### REPL
173	
174	- Prompt `minisql> ` when the buffer is empty, `   ...> ` otherwise; written to stdout without newline, flushed, whether or not stdin is a TTY. Input is not echoed.
175	- With an empty buffer, a line whose stripped text starts with `.` is a command; a blank line is ignored. Otherwise the line is appended (joined with `\n`); when the buffer, right-stripped, ends with `;`, it is executed and cleared.
176	- Commands: `.help` (free text), `.tables` (one name per line, `tables()` order), `.schema NAME` (`name TYPE` per line), `.format csv|table`, `.quit` and `.exit`. Unknown command: stderr `unknown command: <text>`.
177	- Results print in the current format (CSV has no row-count footer). Errors print one line to stderr and the session continues; positions are relative to the buffer.
178	- At EOF a non-empty buffer is executed; then exit 0 with nothing further printed. `.quit` exits 0.
179	
180	### Exit codes (one-shot)
181	
182	| Code | Meaning |
183	|---|---|
184	| 0 | success |
185	| 1 | LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, RuntimeError |
186	| 2 | usage error (argparse) |
187	| 3 | IOError |
188	
189	On error stdout is empty and stderr holds exactly the error line plus `\n`. No tracebacks.
190	
191	## Error handling
192	
193	Classes exported from `minisql`, subclassing `MiniSQLError(Exception)`: `LexError`, `ParseError`, `SemanticError`, `QueryRuntimeError`, `DataIOError`, with attributes `kind` (`Lex`/`Parse`/`Semantic`/`Runtime`/`IO`), `line`, `column` (`None` for IO), `message`; `str(err)` is the formatted line.
194	
195	Format: `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; IO errors: `IOError: <message>`.
196	
197	| Kind | Message templates | Position |
198	|---|---|---|
199	| Lex | `unexpected character 'X'`, `unterminated string literal`, `unterminated quoted identifier`, `invalid number literal` | offending character / opening quote / literal start |
200	| Parse | `unexpected token 'T'` (T = token source text), `unexpected end of input` | token start / one past last input character |
201	| Semantic | `unknown table 'N'`, `duplicate table name 'N'`, `unknown column 'R'`, `ambiguous column 'R'`, `unknown function 'F'`, `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT`, `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T1 and T2`, `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T`, `condition must be numeric, got TEXT`, `aggregate function not allowed here`, `column 'R' must appear in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate`, `'*' not allowed in aggregate query`, `ORDER BY position N is out of range`, `ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used`, `ESCAPE must be a single character` | table/name token; column ref start; operator token (function name for aggregates); condition/expression start; `*`; ordinal; ESCAPE string |
202	| Runtime | `division by zero`, `invalid LIKE pattern` | `/` or `%` token; `LIKE` token |
203	| IO | `data directory not found: DIR` (DIR as given), `ambiguous table file 'N'`, `<file>: empty file`, `<file>: empty column name`, `<file>: duplicate column 'C'`, `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M`, `<file>: line N: malformed CSV`, `<file>: invalid UTF-8` | none |
204	
205	`N`, `R`, `F` are names as written in the query without quotes (`R` qualified as `q.c`). `OP` is the operator as written for symbols, upper-case for keywords and aggregates (`LIKE`, `IN`, `AND`, `SUM`). `<file>` is the base file name. For `duplicate table name 'N'`, the position is the range-name token of the second `tableref` with that range name (its alias if present, else its table name) and `N` is that range name as written. For `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT`, the position is the `*` token inside the call. For `duplicate column 'C'`, `C` is the second occurrence's header name exactly as written in the CSV. For `malformed CSV`, `N` is the reader's `line_num` at the moment `csv.Error` is raised. Phases run lex → parse → semantic (including IO for referenced tables, in `FROM` order) → execute. The oracle only uses queries containing a single error.
206	
207	## Acceptance criteria
208	
209	Fixture `emp.csv`: `id,name,dept,salary` / `1,Ann,eng,100` / `2,Bob,eng,` / `3,Cid,ops,80` / `4,Dee,,80` / `5,Eve,ops,120`. Fixture `dept.csv`: `code,title` / `eng,Engineering` / `ops,Operations` / `ops,Ops Dup` / `hr,Human Resources`.
210	
211	- **AC1** (R1, R19) `python -m minisql --data D "SELECT 1 AS one"` prints `one\n1\n`, exit 0; no non-stdlib or `sqlite3` import in `minisql/`.
212	- **AC2** (R2, R21) `SELECT * FROM EMP` returns 5 rows; `--data missing` exits 3 with `IOError: data directory not found: missing`.
213	- **AC3** (R3) `schema("emp")` is `[("id","INTEGER"),("name","TEXT"),("dept","TEXT"),("salary","INTEGER")]`.
214	- **AC4** (R4, R21) `SELECT 1 # 2` → `LexError at line 1, column 10: unexpected character '#'`.
215	- **AC5** (R5) `SELECT 1 + 2 * 3, -2 * 3, NOT 1 = 2` → `1 + 2 * 3,-2 * 3,NOT 1 = 2` / `7,-6,1`.
216	- **AC6** (R6) `select NAME from Emp e where E.Id = 1` → `name` / `Ann` (header from the CSV, not the query).
217	- **AC7** (R7) `SELECT name + 1 FROM emp` → `SemanticError at line 1, column 13: type mismatch: cannot apply '+' to TEXT and INTEGER`.
218	- **AC8** (R8) `SELECT 7 / 2, -7 / 2, 7 % -2, 7.0 / 2, NULL / 0` → `3,-3,1,3.5,`.
219	- **AC9** (R9) `SELECT name FROM emp WHERE dept NOT IN ('eng', NULL)` → header only.
220	- **AC10** (R10) `SELECT salary * 2, name AS n FROM emp WHERE id = 1` → header `salary * 2,n`, row `200,Ann`.
221	- **AC11** (R17) `connect(D).execute("SELECT AVG(salary) FROM emp")` has `types == ["REAL"]`, `rows == [(95.0,)]`.
222	- **AC12** (R2-R21) Behaviour specified in the Language reference, Interface contract and Error handling sections is reproduced exactly (byte-for-byte output, exit codes and error lines) by hidden tests.
223	"}]}]

"1	# AGENTS.md — geeky-orchestration
2	
3	Guidance for **any** AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Windsurf,
4	Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, or an SDK/LangGraph orchestrator) working with this
5	plugin's plan → execute → track workflow. Claude Code reads this via `@AGENTS.md`;
6	most other CLI agents read `AGENTS.md` natively.
7	
8	## Eval operator readiness
9	
10	This section applies only to operators in the source checkout. Contestant exports deliberately omit `evals/`; exported contestants must follow the canonical authorization and exported skills without looking for these operator files or adding a new approval gate. For source-checkout C0 preparation, read [current readiness](evals/c0-readiness.md) and [lessons learned](evals/lessons-learned.md). Generate fresh offline inventory and verify its exact HEAD, source hashes and prompt hash before a separately authorized live action. Local inventory and mock success grant no launch or telemetry publication authority. Preserve historical evidence and scores. Record desired and observed model/effort by role, the authorization reference, attempt/recovery limits, reserve and existing qualification waiver. Once a particular contestant run is authorized, retain the end-to-end workflow permissions already granted by its canonical prompt.
11	
12	## The workflow
13	
14	1. **spec-research** — research and write `feature-specification.md`.
15	2. **geeky-plan** — create the frozen planning package.
16	3. **plan-review** — validate alignment, coverage, sequencing, and readiness.
17	4. **geeky-status** — read-only status and resumption orientation at any packet stage.
18	5. **geeky-implement** — execute Ready tasks with validation and review gates.
19	6. **impl-review** — review delivered code through three domain-specific lanes.
20	7. **archive** — move completed planning artifacts into the archive structure.
21	
22	Use **geeky-orchestrator** when the requested entry point is unclear or when one
23	agent should administer the lifecycle. It examines repository evidence read-only
24	and recommends a workflow before mutation. Clear, explicit requests route to the
25	best matching skill after prerequisite checks. Material ambiguity is clarified;
26	stages are not auto-chained without end-to-end authorization.
27	
28	Full procedures live in the portable Skills under `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
29	
30	## Workflow terminology
31	
32	Use these meanings across skills, briefs and reports. They describe the orchestration
33	domain; retain the target project's own domain language. Existing filenames, schema
34	fields and checkpoint markers remain unchanged.
35	
36	| Term | Meaning |
37	|---|---|
38	| Planning package | Specification, plan, task contracts and tracking artifacts for one approved outcome. "Packet" is an alias; planning folder is its location. |
39	| Workflow stage | A lifecycle activity such as planning, implementation or final implementation review. Numbered "phases" inside a skill are procedure steps, not implementation phases. |
40	| Implementation phase | A group of tasks whose combined requirements are reviewed before advancement. "Wave" means a scheduling group unless the plan explicitly equates it with a phase. |
41	| Task | A bounded unit with an ID, scope, dependencies, acceptance criteria (ACs) and required validation. |
42	| Requirement / AC / Definition of Done | Required outcome or constraint / observable condition for satisfying it / completion conditions for the task. Required tests supply evidence; they do not replace ACs. |
43	| Task contract | The frozen task body and applicable approved requirements. A task brief conveys that contract to a worker. |
44	| Validation | Checks of the work. Validation evidence records what ran or was observed, against which inputs, and the result; a PASS claim alone is not evidence. |
45	| Review | Judgment of evidence against an assigned scope. Task review checks ACs/tests; phase review decides readiness to advance; final implementation review uses `impl-review`. Plan review evaluates the planning package. |
46	| Acceptance | The decision that required outcomes and gates for the stated scope are satisfied. Task Done, phase READY TO ADVANCE and final review PASS have different scopes; none grants release or deployment approval. |
47	| Finding | An evidenced discrepancy. A blocking finding prevents the current contract from being met; an optional improvement is a follow-up. Severity labels retain their review-stage meanings, not an automatic cross-stage mapping. |
48	| Execution batch / review batch | Tasks dispatched together / tasks sharing a reviewer assignment. Each phase has one review batch, the phase review: members wait in In Review until it clears, and each keeps its own verdict. |
49	| Orchestrator / worker / reviewer | Coordinates and accepts work / performs a bounded assignment / evaluates it. `geeky-coder` is the implementation worker; PM describes a planning or phase-review perspective. |
50	
51	## The planning-folder contract
52	
53	**Frozen** (never edit mid-run — they are the contract between plan and implement):
54	`implementation-plan.md`, `feature-specification.md`, `draft.md`, `references.md`,

61

67	Every gate: **arguments in, exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, summary on stdout**,
68	optional `--json` / `-Json`. Each ships paired Python + PowerShell with identical
69	behavior. `geeky.manifest.json` is the machine-readable index of the same list.
70	
71	Paths below are relative to this plugin root (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in Claude Code).
72	Use `python3` where `python` is not on PATH; use `pwsh` (PowerShell 7+) for the `.ps1`.
73	
74	| Gate | When | Python | PowerShell |
75	|---|---|---|---|
76	| Planning-folder valid | start of implement/status | `python scripts/validate-planning-folder.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-planning-folder.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
77	| Task-file schema | end of plan; start of implement | `python scripts/validate-task-schema.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-task-schema.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
78	| Kanban integrity | after every lane move | `python scripts/validate-kanban.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-kanban.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
79	| Definition of Done | in the Done step: move the task to Done, run this gate in the same step, move it back out on failure (D92) | `python scripts/check-dod.py --path "<folder>" --task <ID>` | `pwsh -File scripts/check-dod.ps1 -Path "<folder>" -Task <ID>` |
80	| Commit message | before each commit; pre-planning docs commits use `Tasks: none` | `python scripts/check-commit.py --message "<msg>"` (or `<FILE>`) | `pwsh -File scripts/check-commit.ps1 -Message "<msg>"` (or `<FILE>`) |
81	
82	**Feedback loop:** when a gate exits non-zero, read its output, fix the artifact,
83	and re-run the same gate until it exits 0 before proceeding.
84	
85	## How each agent type runs the gates
86	
87	- **Claude Code:** the frozen-artifact guard fires automatically via
88	  `hooks/hooks.json` (PreToolUse). Run the validators above as explicit steps.
89	- **Other CLI agents (Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Gemini):** add an
90	  equivalent pre-edit/stop hook in your tool's config pointing at
91	  `hooks/guard-planning-contract.{py,ps1}` (it reads tool-call JSON on stdin,

98	  `geeky_validate_task_schema`, `geeky_validate_kanban`, `geeky_check_dod`,
99	  `geeky_check_commit`, `geeky_check_frozen_artifact` — for tool-style invocation with

101	  (or `pip install mcp && python mcp/server.py`).
102	
103	## Hard rules for implement
104	
105	Never push to a remote. Never `--no-verify`, `--force`, or `--amend`. Respect each
106	task's declared `Dependencies:`. Stop and finalize state (kanban + handoff) when a
107	task moves to Blocked. Verify task validation evidence against the tested revision,

"## Reader defaults and strict mode

[`csv.reader`](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/csv.html#csv.reader) defaults to `dialect='excel'`. The documented [formatting defaults](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/csv.html#dialects-and-formatting-parameters) are:

| Parameter | Default |
|---|---|
| `delimiter` | `','` |
| `quotechar` | `'"'` |
| `doublequote` | `True` |
| `escapechar` | `None` |
| `quoting` | `csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL` |
| `skipinitialspace` | `False` |
| `strict` | `False` |
| `lineterminator` | `'\r\n'`—writer setting; ignored by the reader |

The reader documentation states:

> “Each row read from the csv file is returned as a list of strings. No automatic data type conversion is performed unless the `QUOTE_NONNUMERIC` format option is specified (in which case unquoted fields are transformed into floats).”

For [`strict`](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/csv.html#csv.Dialect.strict):

> “When `True`, raise exception `Error` on bad CSV input. The default is `False`.”

For [`csv.Error`](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/csv.html#csv.Error):

> “Raised by any of the functions when an error is detected.”

```python
with open("input.csv", newline="") as f:
    reader = csv.reader(f, strict=True)
```

## `newline=''` and embedded newlines

The [`reader` documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/csv.html#csv.reader) says file objects should be opened with `newline=''`. [Footnote 1](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/csv.html#id4) explains:

> “If `newline=''` is not specified, newlines embedded inside quoted fields will not be interpreted correctly, and on platforms that use `\r\n` linendings on write an extra `\r` will be added.”

> “It should always be safe to specify `newline=''`, since the csv module does its own (universal) newline handling.”

The [`lineterminator` section](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/csv.html#csv.Dialect.lineterminator) additionally states:

> “The `reader` is hard-coded to recognise either `'\r'` or `'\n'` as end-of-line, and ignores `lineterminator`.”

## Physical lines versus records

For [`reader.line_num`](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/csv.html#csv.csvreader.line_num):

> “The number of lines read from the source iterator. This is not the same as the number of records returned, as records can span multiple lines.”

Thus, `line_num` is not a record counter, particularly when quoted fields contain embedded newlines.

## Writer defaults, `None`, and empty strings

For [`lineterminator`](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/csv.html#csv.Dialect.lineterminator):

> “The string used to terminate lines produced by the `writer`. It defaults to `'\r\n'`.”

Default [`QUOTE_MINIMAL`](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/csv.html#csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL):

> “Instructs `writer` objects to only quote those fields which contain special characters such as *delimiter*, *quotechar* or any of the characters in *lineterminator*.”

For [`csv.writer`](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/csv.html#csv.writer):

> “the value `None` is written as the empty string.”

> “While this isn’t a reversible transformation, it makes it easier to dump SQL NULL data values to CSV files without preprocessing the data returned from a `cursor.fetch*` call.”

Consequently, writing does not preserve a distinction between `None` and `''`.

## Empty-row specification gap

The supplied page **does not explicitly specify**:

- What `csv.reader` returns for an empty physical line.
- Exact output for `writerow([])` versus `writerow([''])` or `writerow([None])`.
- Special quoting behavior for a single empty field.

The relevant [`DictReader`](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/csv.html#csv.DictReader) statement is narrower:

> “If a non-blank row has fewer fields than fieldnames, the missing values are filled-in with the value of *restval* (which defaults to `None`).”

That statement does not establish ordinary `csv.reader` empty-row behavior; these edge cases are not fully defined by this page’s prose alone."

observations.output:
"## Authoritative Python 3.11 statements

### Encoding defaults — [`TextIOWrapper`](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/io.html#io.TextIOWrapper)

> “*encoding* gives the name of the encoding that the stream will be decoded or encoded with. It defaults to `locale.getencoding()`.”

The [Text Encoding](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/io.html#text-encoding) section also notes that **Python UTF-8 Mode can change the default to UTF-8** and recommends specifying encoding explicitly. For deterministic behavior, use `encoding="utf-8"` rather than relying on the locale or UTF-8 Mode.

### Reading: `newline` — [`TextIOWrapper`](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/io.html#io.TextIOWrapper)

- **`None`**:
  > “Lines in the input can end in `'\n'`, `'\r'`, or `'\r\n'`, and these are translated into `'\n'` before being returned to the caller.”
- **`""`**:
  > “universal newlines mode is enabled, but line endings are returned to the caller untranslated.”
- **`"\n"`, `"\r"`, or `"\r\n"`**:
  > “input lines are only terminated by the given string, and the line ending is returned to the caller untranslated.”

### Writing: `newline` — [`TextIOWrapper`](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/io.html#io.TextIOWrapper)

> “if *newline* is `None`, any `'\n'` characters written are translated to the system default line separator, `os.linesep`.”

> “If *newline* is `''` or `'\n'`, no translation takes place.”

For `"\r"` or `"\r\n"`, written `"\n"` characters are translated to that string.

**Important:** `newline="\n"` prevents platform-dependent translation; it does **not** normalize existing `"\r"` or `"\r\n"` characters in strings you write.

### Reconfiguration — [`TextIOWrapper.reconfigure()`](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/io.html#io.TextIOWrapper.reconfigure)

```python
stream.reconfigure(
    encoding=None, errors=None, newline=None,
    line_buffering=None, write_through=None
)
```

All parameters are keyword-only.

> “Parameters not specified keep current settings, except `errors='strict'` is used when *encoding* is specified but *errors* is not specified.”

> “It is not possible to change the encoding or newline if some data has already been read from the stream. On the other hand, changing encoding after write is possible.”

> “This method does an implicit stream flush before setting the new parameters.”

## Practical settings

### UTF-8 and LF output on Windows/macOS/Linux

```python
with open("output.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as f:
    f.write("first\nsecond\n")
```

### Standard output

The supplied page identifies `sys.stdout` as a standard I/O stream, but **does not explicitly document stdout reconfiguration**. Applying the documented method, **if `sys.stdout` is a `TextIOWrapper`**:

```python
import sys

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
```

Replaced stdout objects, such as `StringIO`, need not support this method.

### CSV: preserve embedded CR/LF, use LF record separators

The following is an application of the documented newline behavior, **not a CSV-specific excerpt from this page**:

```python
import csv

with open("input.csv", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as src, \
     open("output.csv", "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as dst:
    reader = csv.reader(src)
    writer = csv.writer(
        dst, lineterminator="\n", quoting=csv.QUOTE_ALL
    )
    writer.writerows(reader)
```

`newline=""` leaves embedded CR/LF untranslated. `lineterminator="\n"` selects LF **between records**; `QUOTE_ALL` ensures fields containing CR remain quoted even with an LF-only record terminator. Preserving embedded CR/LF means the resulting file is not necessarily LF-only everywhere."

**Status:** Spec written — not yet planned
**Dependencies:** Python 3.11+ standard library; pytest for tests only
**Layer:** Query engine / library / CLI
**Priority:** Critical path: all contract requirements
**Estimated Complexity:** 6–8 bounded tasks across 3 implementation phases (planning to finalize)

## 1. Executive Summary

Implement a handwritten, read-only SQL engine over CSV files, with a flat `minisql/` package, library API, deterministic CSV/table rendering, one-shot CLI and REPL. `../../contract.md` is authoritative in full, including R1–R21 and AC12. This document organizes that contract; it does not narrow or replace it. `../../brief.md` additionally requires recognizable tokenizer, AST parser, semantic analyzer and executor layers and pytest tests.

Research completed with three independent researchers: repository/acceptance analyst `af392ba25adfa556c`, language/semantics researcher `a483bed12b1e836ca`, data/interface researcher `ae056d83d393a869d`. See `research.md` for findings, sources and limitations.

## 2. Problem Statement

### Current State

The seed repository has only `brief.md`, `contract.md` and `.gitignore`; no application, tests or repository-local AGENTS/CLAUDE guidance. No existing integration surface or prior spec convention constrains module names beyond the required package layout. [Research: repository analyst; contract constraints]

### Impact of Inaction

There is no executable engine or API. A generic SQL approximation would fail the bespoke arithmetic, source naming, aggregate legality, error and exact-output requirements. Every explicit rule, not merely AC1–AC11, is required by AC12.

## 3. Goals & Non-Goals

### Goals

- Implement all R1–R21 and exact AC1–AC12 behavior.
- Expose `python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]` and `minisql.connect(DIR).execute(SQL)`.
- Use Python >=3.11, stdlib runtime imports only; no sqlite3, existing SQL engine or parser.
- Deterministic ordering, UTF-8/LF output, exact classes/messages/positions, no partial one-shot output or tracebacks for specified failures.
- Contract-derived pytest coverage including errors, empty inputs, stage ordering, byte-level CLI/REPL and data edge cases.

### Non-goals

Writes, DDL, subqueries, SQL beyond the supplied grammar, database compatibility, third-party runtime dependencies, query optimizations that change required evaluation, network services, release/deploy/publication.

**Assumption:** portability is implemented through standard-library behavior and tested locally; unavailable OS/runtime executions must be reported, not claimed.

## 4. Architecture

Proposed separable surfaces (planning may refine file names, never required behavior):

1. Errors and immutable-shaped Result API.
2. Lexer: complete token stream with source offsets and positions.
3. Parser/AST: handwritten recursive descent matching contract grammar and precedence, retaining parentheses and source spans.
4. Catalog/loader: directory validation, discovery, strict CSV reading, whole-column inference.
5. Semantic binder: scoped names, resolved column identity, static types, aggregate legality, structural grouping/DISTINCT/ORDER validation.
6. Executor: explicit ordered materialized stages, typed nullable values, aggregate collection, stable sort.
7. Formatters and CLI/REPL: pure formatting separate from transport and stream configuration.

`connect` validates the directory immediately. Thereafter execute follows lex → parse → semantic (including referenced-table IO in FROM order) → execute. Binding completes before any row expression is evaluated, including empty/unreachable branches. Do not stream output until execute and formatting succeed. [Contract R7, R16–R21; lines 113, 138–143, 189, 205]

## 5. Detailed Design

### 5.1 Data and schema (R2–R3)

- Discover only direct regular files with case-insensitive `.csv` extension; table name is stem, lookup case-insensitive. Colliding lowercase stems raise `ambiguous table file` only when referenced. `tables()` returns stems sorted by `(lower(), name)` without opening content.
- Read referenced files anew per execute using `encoding='utf-8-sig'`, `newline=''`, `csv.reader(..., strict=True)` default dialect. Never read unrelated files. Preserve raw contents, BOM handling, quoted CR/LF and whitespace.
- Skip zero-field records, choose first nonzero-field record as header (decision D1). Header names verbatim; reject empty names and case-insensitive duplicates using second occurrence spelling.
- Enforce record width using reader.line_num after the record. Catch csv.Error with its current reader.line_num; invalid UTF-8 has the fixed template.
- Inference scans every nonempty field without trimming. Full ASCII integer regex first; else full contract REAL regex; else TEXT verbatim. Empty raw field → None; all-empty column → TEXT. Convert numeric-looking strings only once whole-column type is known.

Sources: contract lines 105–116; Python csv reader/line_num and TextIOWrapper documentation in `research.md`.

### 5.2 Lexing and parsing (R4–R6)

Implement the exact EBNF and precedence in contract lines 36–86. Reserved keywords are exactly the listed set; aggregate function names remain ordinary identifiers. Names and keywords resolve case-insensitively using `lower()`, while source spelling is retained.

Whitespace is space/tab/CR/LF only; `--` ends at LF. Only LF advances line. Tabs, CR and Unicode each count one code point. Quoted identifiers allow doubled double quotes and arbitrary content. Strings allow doubled single quotes, multiline content and literal backslashes.

Recognize integer and real forms using ASCII digit patterns. A number immediately followed by ASCII alphanumeric, underscore or dot is invalid at the literal start. Signs are unary. Comparisons/predicates are non-associative; chained comparisons fail at the second operator. Calls accept exactly one expression or star. IN is nonempty. FROM is optional (one empty row). LIMIT/OFFSET accept only unsigned integer literal tokens; OFFSET is independently optional; at most one terminal semicolon.

Retain token raw source, decoded value, span, line/column, and AST parentheses. Parentheses affect output names and bare ORDER recognition, but not structural identity (D5).

### 5.3 Static typing and operators (R7–R9)

Types: INTEGER/int, REAL/float, TEXT/str, NULL for bare NULL-derived null expressions. Values may be None; predicates return 1/0/None, never bool.

- Numeric arithmetic accepts INTEGER/REAL/NULL; REAL wins, else both NULL → NULL, else INTEGER. Unary signs retain operand type.
- Comparisons and each IN item require numeric pairs, TEXT pairs, or either NULL type. TEXT uses Python code-point order.
- LIKE accepts TEXT/NULL. Logical operands and WHERE/ON/HAVING conditions must be numeric/NULL.
- NULL arithmetic propagates before zero-divisor checking. Exact integer quotient truncates toward zero without float conversion; remainder is dividend-signed. REAL remainder uses math.fmod.
- Full 3VL: NULL comparisons unknown; IS returns integer boolean. AND short-circuits only false LHS; OR only true LHS; NULL LHS still evaluates RHS.
- IN truth results follow contract; evaluate all non-NULL-LHS list items left-to-right before membership decision (D3). NULL LHS returns NULL.
- LIKE is whole-string, case-sensitive, supports newline/Unicode. `%` any sequence, `_` one character. ESCAPE is one-character STRING checked statically. Invalid escaped pattern sequence or trailing escape is runtime at LIKE; NULL operands return NULL first.

Sources: contract lines 88–103. SUM/AVG NULL-type policy is recorded in D2, not borrowed from another SQL dialect.

### 5.4 Resolution, projection and joins (R6, R10–R11)

Bind columns to stable resolved table/column identities. Unqualified search spans current visible ranges; zero matches unknown, multiple ambiguous. Alias hides original table qualifier. Reject duplicate range names at the second range-name token. Each ON sees only its join prefix.

Expand `*`/`q.*` in FROM/header order; output duplicates are legal. Name outputs by explicit alias, else unparenthesized column's exact CSV header, else exact first-to-last item-expression source slice (not alias text). No implicit output-name namespace for WHERE/GROUP/HAVING.

Joins associate left with literal nested loops: left rows outer, right file rows inner; evaluate ON on every pair, retain true only. LEFT unmatched rows append one NULL-filled right side. NULL never equals NULL in ON.

Sources: contract lines 74, 118–122, 140.

### 5.5 Aggregation and grouping (R12)

Aggregate query if GROUP BY, HAVING, or any aggregate call in SELECT/ORDER BY (HAVING itself establishes aggregate mode). COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(e) non-NULL; SUM INTEGER/REAL preserves numeric type; AVG REAL; MIN/MAX retain argument type. All ignore NULL, COUNT empty → 0, others → None. Only COUNT accepts star. SUM/AVG accept NULL as numeric-compatible (D2); SUM(NULL) type NULL, AVG(NULL) REAL.

No GROUP BY → one global group even after empty WHERE. Explicit grouping over empty input → zero groups. First-seen group order; None equals None for keys. Collect every aggregate across SELECT/HAVING/ORDER. Evaluate group keys and aggregate arguments for surviving input rows before HAVING. Do not lazily defer arguments until projection.

Select/HAVING/ORDER expressions must recursively consist of aggregate calls, literals and subexpressions structurally identical to a GROUP key. Match resolved columns, normalized keyword operators, typed literal values and operand order. Parentheses are transparent; alternate numeric spellings of same type/value match. Do not perform algebraic normalization or conflate `!=` and `<>` (D5). No star projections in aggregate queries; no aggregates in WHERE/ON/GROUP or inside an aggregate.

Sources: contract lines 124–129, 138–143.

### 5.6 Ordering, DISTINCT and slicing (R13–R16)

- Bare INTEGER ORDER expression is 1-based ordinal after star expansion. `(1)`, `+1`, REAL literals are expressions, not ordinals.
- Bare unqualified identifier matching exactly one explicit select alias refers to that output, taking precedence over input; two aliases → ambiguity. Otherwise bind input/group expression.
- DISTINCT ORDER must be ordinal, alias or structurally equal to a select expression.
- Evaluate stages exactly: FROM/joins → WHERE → all group keys/aggregate arguments → HAVING → projection → ORDER keys → first-occurrence DISTINCT → stable multi-key sort → OFFSET → LIMIT.
- NULL smallest; ascending first, descending last. Stable descending ties too. Numeric comparisons mixed freely; text by Python str ordering.
- LIMIT 0 does not suppress earlier evaluation/failures. OFFSET past end returns zero rows.

Sources: contract lines 131–143.

### 5.7 API and formatting (R17–R18)

Export connect, Connection, frozen dataclass Result(columns: list[str], types: list[str], rows: list[tuple]), format_csv, format_table and all required errors. connect accepts str/PathLike; schema returns `(header, type)` tuples in header order. No import-time changes to host streams.

INTEGER uses str, REAL repr, TEXT verbatim. CSV custom quoting: NULL empty/unquoted; empty string quoted; quote iff empty string, comma, quote, CR/LF, or starts/ends with literal space; double internal quotes. Headers same. Every record LF.

Table: escape actual CR/LF to visible `\\r`/`\\n` before width measurement; same for headers (D4). Width code points; header left, numeric values right, TEXT/NULL left. Join with ` | `; separator `-+-`; strip trailing spaces on every line; `(N rows)`/`(1 row)`; final LF.

Sources: contract lines 145–170; Python io docs.

### 5.8 CLI and REPL (R19–R20)

Configure CLI stdout/stderr UTF-8 with LF (not at library import). argparse usage errors exit 2 (D6). Missing/non-directory data fails before SQL lexing, exit 3. Query failures exit 1; success 0. Complete result before writing; error stdout empty and stderr exact single error line plus LF.

No SQL → REPL, default table; one-shot default CSV; explicit --format overrides either. Prompt always stdout flushed even non-TTY: `minisql> ` empty buffer else `   ...> `. Empty-buffer blank input ignored; stripped dot-prefix line is command. Other lines append joined LF. Execute/clear when right-stripped buffer ends `;`, without SQL-aware completion. Commands .help, .tables, .schema NAME, .format csv|table, .quit/.exit. Unknown command fixed stderr text. Errors continue. EOF executes nonempty buffer then returns 0 with no further output; prompt already emitted before EOF remains.

Sources: contract lines 168–189.

### 5.9 Errors (R21)

Implement every template and position in contract lines 191–205 verbatim. Export MiniSQLError(Exception), LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, QueryRuntimeError, DataIOError; kind Lex/Parse/Semantic/Runtime/IO; message and line/column attributes (both None for IO). SQL string format `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; IO `IOError: <message>`.

Names in errors preserve query spelling without quotes; refs qualified as q.c. Operators keywords and aggregate names uppercase; symbols as written. Duplicate range name at second alias/table name token; call star error at internal star; invalid ESCAPE length at string; division at operator; invalid LIKE at LIKE. EOF at one past last source character, with LF-only position accounting. IO file names basenames. Single-error oracle means no invented tie-break requirements among unrelated competing semantic errors.

## 6. Cost Estimates

No external service/package costs. Primary cost is implementation and contract-edge testing. No optional web expansion needed. Runtime availability risk: default available Python is 3.9.6; installed 3.14 and 3.14-intel64 exit via SIGKILL (-9) before `--version`. Do not install without authorization; test on available runtime with a clearly recorded supported-runtime gap if no working >=3.11 is found. Product must remain Python 3.11+ compatible regardless.

## 7. Task Outline (Preliminary)

1. Foundation: errors, result, tokens, AST/parser and catalog/inference (independent surfaces).
2. Typed binding and execution: static resolution/typing, grouping/order legality, full stage pipeline and operators.
3. Interfaces and integration: API, formatters, CLI/REPL, comprehensive regression and acceptance traceability.

Planning will define non-overlapping task contracts, dependencies, validations and phase gates; each phase requires independent reviewer READY TO ADVANCE and task evidence.

## 8. Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Generic SQL assumptions diverge | Contract-derived tests; no SQL engine oracle |
| Lost source/bare metadata | Retain token and AST spans/parentheses; separate structural keys |
| Lazy/fused execution changes error order | Explicit materialized stage barriers and fault-order tests |
| Incorrect nullable static types | Bind before execute; test empty/unreachable branches |
| Group matching too permissive | Resolved structural keys; no algebraic rewrites |
| CSV newline/physical-line changes | Required open/reader configuration; byte fixtures |
| Cross-platform output drift | Custom quote function, stream reconfigure, golden bytes |
| Host runtime limits | Record exact failed launch evidence and local runtime; do not claim unrun platforms |

### Recorded decisions and alternatives

All decisions are also in mutable `handoff.md`. They resolve underspecified edges only; explicit contract always wins.

- **D1:** Skip all zero-field CSV records, including before header; first nonempty record is header. Alternative: literal first record header. Reason: general skip rule is closest evidence.
- **D2:** NULL is permitted for SUM/AVG as numeric-compatible; SUM(NULL) has NULL static type, AVG(NULL) REAL; both value None. Alternative: reject bare NULL as nonnumeric. Reason: consistent NULL operand acceptance and all-null aggregate outcomes; no defined SUM(NULL) type otherwise.
- **D3:** IN with NULL LHS returns NULL; otherwise evaluate all items left-to-right before deciding membership. Alternative: stop at first match. Reason: only AND/OR explicitly authorize short circuit; avoid hiding failures.
- **D4:** Escape CR/LF in table headers as in cell text. Alternative: retain literal newlines. Reason: headers are cells and aligned table remains deterministic.
- **D5:** Structural keys ignore parentheses/source spelling, compare typed literal value, preserve symbol spelling and operand order; lowercase resolved names. Alternative: source-text keys / normalize comparison synonyms. Reason: same resolved columns/operators/literals, no algebraic extension.
- **D6:** Standard argparse usage diagnostics apply to exit 2; exact single-line engine-error requirement applies to specified query/data errors. Malformed dot-command arguments use unknown-command text. schema unknown table uses SemanticError at 1:1. Unlisted OS read failures become DataIOError with stable basename and OS description where possible. Alternative: invent new templates. Reason: preserve defined behavior; no new public query error template.
- **D7:** No runtime installation; use available tests and report unsupported-runtime/platform execution honestly. Alternative: external installation. Reason: no external-install authority and no need to change product constraints.

No researchers disagreed on an explicit requirement. Unresolved policies and alternatives above are orchestrator decisions, not changes to contract authority.

## 9. Acceptance Criteria

All R1–R21 and AC1–AC12 in `../../contract.md` are mandatory, with a test matrix covering each detailed section. Required anchors include:

- AC1 CLI `SELECT 1 AS one`: bytes `one\n1\n`, exit 0; stdlib import audit.
- AC2 EMP returns 5 rows; missing data exact IO line and exit 3.
- AC3 emp schema INTEGER/TEXT/TEXT/INTEGER.
- AC4 `SELECT 1 # 2`: LexError line 1 column 10.
- AC5 precedence yields 7,-6,1 with exact expression headings.
- AC6 case-insensitive names preserve CSV heading `name`, row Ann.
- AC7 TEXT arithmetic SemanticError at '+' column 13, before execution.
- AC8 integer/real division/remainder and NULL division yield 3,-3,1,3.5,None.
- AC9 NOT IN with NULL yields header only.
- AC10 source heading `salary * 2,n`, row 200,Ann.
- AC11 AVG salary result types [REAL], rows [(95.0,)].
- AC12 all lexical, grammar, type, data, join, aggregate, order, format, protocol and error rules, including edge tests in `research.md`.

Test evidence must include numeric pytest counts, exact commands/runtime, import/compile checks and subprocess byte assertions. A worker PASS alone is insufficient. No acceptance is established by budget checks.

## 10. Dependencies on Prior Features

None. Test dependency pytest only; runtime stdlib. No existing code to preserve. Workflow validators and frozen planning contract apply once planning completes.

## 11. Delegation to Future Specs

No required functionality deferred. Performance optimization, writes, additional SQL, release packaging, external CI platforms and installation are outside this feature. Host-specific test execution gaps are warnings, not silent claims of completion.

The seed repository has only `brief.md`, `contract.md` and `.gitignore`; no application, tests or repository-local AGENTS/CLAUDE guidance. No existing integration surface or prior spec convention constrains module names beyond the required package layout. [Research: repository analyst; contract constraints]

### Impact of Inaction

There is no executable engine or API. A generic SQL approximation would fail the bespoke arithmetic, source naming, aggregate legality, error and exact-output requirements. Every explicit rule, not merely AC1–AC11, is required by AC12.

## 3. Goals & Non-Goals

### Goals

- Implement all R1–R21 and exact AC1–AC12 behavior.
- Expose `python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]` and `minisql.connect(DIR).execute(SQL)`.
- Use Python >=3.11, stdlib runtime imports only; no sqlite3, existing SQL engine or parser.
- Deterministic ordering, UTF-8/LF output, exact classes/messages/positions, no partial one-shot output or tracebacks for specified failures.
- Contract-derived pytest coverage including errors, empty inputs, stage ordering, byte-level CLI/REPL and data edge cases.

### Non-goals

Writes, DDL, subqueries, SQL beyond the supplied grammar, database compatibility, third-party runtime dependencies, query optimizations that change required evaluation, network services, release/deploy/publication.

**Assumption:** portability is implemented through standard-library behavior and tested locally; unavailable OS/runtime executions must be reported, not claimed.

## 4. Architecture

Proposed separable surfaces (planning may refine file names, never required behavior):

1. Errors and immutable-shaped Result API.
2. Lexer: complete token stream with source offsets and positions.
3. Parser/AST: handwritten recursive descent matching contract grammar and precedence, retaining parentheses and source spans.
4. Catalog/loader: directory validation, discovery, strict CSV reading, whole-column inference.
5. Semantic binder: scoped names, resolved column identity, static types, aggregate legality, structural grouping/DISTINCT/ORDER validation.
6. Executor: explicit ordered materialized stages, typed nullable values, aggregate collection, stable sort.
7. Formatters and CLI/REPL: pure formatting separate from transport and stream configuration.

`connect` validates the directory immediately. Thereafter execute follows lex → parse → semantic (including referenced-table IO in FROM order) → execute. Binding completes before any row expression is evaluated, including empty/unreachable branches. Do not stream output until execute and formatting succeed. [Contract R7, R16–R21; lines 113, 138–143, 189, 205]

## 5. Detailed Design

### 5.1 Data and schema (R2–R3)

- Discover only direct regular files with case-insensitive `.csv` extension; table name is stem, lookup case-insensitive. Colliding lowercase stems raise `ambiguous table file` only when referenced. `tables()` returns stems sorted by `(lower(), name)` without opening content.
- Read referenced files anew per execute using `encoding='utf-8-sig'`, `newline=''`, `csv.reader(..., strict=True)` default dialect. Never read unrelated files. Preserve raw contents, BOM handling, quoted CR/LF and whitespace.
- Skip zero-field records, choose first nonzero-field record as header (decision D1). Header names verbatim; reject empty names and case-insensitive duplicates using second occurrence spelling.
- Enforce record width using reader.line_num after the record. Catch csv.Error with its current reader.line_num; invalid UTF-8 has the fixed template.
- Inference scans every nonempty field without trimming. Full ASCII integer regex first; else full contract REAL regex; else TEXT verbatim. Empty raw field → None; all-empty column → TEXT. Convert numeric-looking strings only once whole-column type is known.

Sources: contract lines 105–116; Python csv reader/line_num and TextIOWrapper documentation in `research.md`.

### 5.2 Lexing and parsing (R4–R6)

Implement the exact EBNF and precedence in contract lines 36–86. Reserved keywords are exactly the listed set; aggregate function names remain ordinary identifiers. Names and keywords resolve case-insensitively using `lower()`, while source spelling is retained.

Whitespace is space/tab/CR/LF only; `--` ends at LF. Only LF advances line. Tabs, CR and Unicode each count one code point. Quoted identifiers allow doubled double quotes and arbitrary content. Strings allow doubled single quotes, multiline content and literal backslashes.

Recognize integer and real forms using ASCII digit patterns. A number immediately followed by ASCII alphanumeric, underscore or dot is invalid at the literal start. Signs are unary. Comparisons/predicates are non-associative; chained comparisons fail at the second operator. Calls accept exactly one expression or star. IN is nonempty. FROM is optional (one empty row). LIMIT/OFFSET accept only unsigned integer literal tokens; OFFSET is independently optional; at most one terminal semicolon.

Retain token raw source, decoded value, span, line/column, and AST parentheses. Parentheses affect output names and bare ORDER recognition, but not structural identity (D5).

### 5.3 Static typing and operators (R7–R9)

Types: INTEGER/int, REAL/float, TEXT/str, NULL for bare NULL-derived null expressions. Values may be None; predicates return 1/0/None, never bool.

- Numeric arithmetic accepts INTEGER/REAL/NULL; REAL wins, else both NULL → NULL, else INTEGER. Unary signs retain operand type.
- Comparisons and each IN item require numeric pairs, TEXT pairs, or either NULL type. TEXT uses Python code-point order.
- LIKE accepts TEXT/NULL. Logical operands and WHERE/ON/HAVING conditions must be numeric/NULL.
- NULL arithmetic propagates before zero-divisor checking. Exact integer quotient truncates toward zero without float conversion; remainder is dividend-signed. REAL remainder uses math.fmod.
- Full 3VL: NULL comparisons unknown; IS returns integer boolean. AND short-circuits only false LHS; OR only true LHS; NULL LHS still evaluates RHS.
- IN truth results follow contract; evaluate all non-NULL-LHS list items left-to-right before membership decision (D3). NULL LHS returns NULL.
- LIKE is whole-string, case-sensitive, supports newline/Unicode. `%` any sequence, `_` one character. ESCAPE is one-character STRING checked statically. Invalid escaped pattern sequence or trailing escape is runtime at LIKE; NULL operands return NULL first.

Sources: contract lines 88–103. SUM/AVG NULL-type policy is recorded in D2, not borrowed from another SQL dialect.

### 5.4 Resolution, projection and joins (R6, R10–R11)

Bind columns to stable resolved table/column identities. Unqualified search spans current visible ranges; zero matches unknown, multiple ambiguous. Alias hides original table qualifier. Reject duplicate range names at the second range-name token. Each ON sees only its join prefix.

Expand `*`/`q.*` in FROM/header order; output duplicates are legal. Name outputs by explicit alias, else unparenthesized column's exact CSV header, else exact first-to-last item-expression source slice (not alias text). No implicit output-name namespace for WHERE/GROUP/HAVING.

Joins associate left with literal nested loops: left rows outer, right file rows inner; evaluate ON on every pair, retain true only. LEFT unmatched rows append one NULL-filled right side. NULL never equals NULL in ON.

Sources: contract lines 74, 118–122, 140.

### 5.5 Aggregation and grouping (R12)

Aggregate query if GROUP BY, HAVING, or any aggregate call in SELECT/ORDER BY (HAVING itself establishes aggregate mode). COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(e) non-NULL; SUM INTEGER/REAL preserves numeric type; AVG REAL; MIN/MAX retain argument type. All ignore NULL, COUNT empty → 0, others → None. Only COUNT accepts star. SUM/AVG accept NULL as numeric-compatible (D2); SUM(NULL) type NULL, AVG(NULL) REAL.

No GROUP BY → one global group even after empty WHERE. Explicit grouping over empty input → zero groups. First-seen group order; None equals None for keys. Collect every aggregate across SELECT/HAVING/ORDER. Evaluate group keys and aggregate arguments for surviving input rows before HAVING. Do not lazily defer arguments until projection.

Select/HAVING/ORDER expressions must recursively consist of aggregate calls, literals and subexpressions structurally identical to a GROUP key. Match resolved columns, normalized keyword operators, typed literal values and operand order. Parentheses are transparent; alternate numeric spellings of same type/value match. Do not perform algebraic normalization or conflate `!=` and `<>` (D5). No star projections in aggregate queries; no aggregates in WHERE/ON/GROUP or inside an aggregate.

Sources: contract lines 124–129, 138–143.

### 5.6 Ordering, DISTINCT and slicing (R13–R16)

- Bare INTEGER ORDER expression is 1-based ordinal after star expansion. `(1)`, `+1`, REAL literals are expressions, not ordinals.
- Bare unqualified identifier matching exactly one explicit select alias refers to that output, taking precedence over input; two aliases → ambiguity. Otherwise bind input/group expression.
- DISTINCT ORDER must be ordinal, alias or structurally equal to a select expression.
- Evaluate stages exactly: FROM/joins → WHERE → all group keys/aggregate arguments → HAVING → projection → ORDER keys → first-occurrence DISTINCT → stable multi-key sort → OFFSET → LIMIT.
- NULL smallest; ascending first, descending last. Stable descending ties too. Numeric comparisons mixed freely; text by Python str ordering.
- LIMIT 0 does not suppress earlier evaluation/failures. OFFSET past end returns zero rows.

Sources: contract lines 131–143.

### 5.7 API and formatting (R17–R18)

Export connect, Connection, frozen dataclass Result(columns: list[str], types: list[str], rows: list[tuple]), format_csv, format_table and all required errors. connect accepts str/PathLike; schema returns `(header, type)` tuples in header order. No import-time changes to host streams.

INTEGER uses str, REAL repr, TEXT verbatim. CSV custom quoting: NULL empty/unquoted; empty string quoted; quote iff empty string, comma, quote, CR/LF, or starts/ends with literal space; double internal quotes. Headers same. Every record LF.

Table: escape actual CR/LF to visible `\\r`/`\\n` before width measurement; same for headers (D4). Width code points; header left, numeric values right, TEXT/NULL left. Join with ` | `; separator `-+-`; strip trailing spaces on every line; `(N rows)`/`(1 row)`; final LF.

Sources: contract lines 145–170; Python io docs.

### 5.8 CLI and REPL (R19–R20)

Configure CLI stdout/stderr UTF-8 with LF (not at library import). argparse usage errors exit 2 (D6). Missing/non-directory data fails before SQL lexing, exit 3. Query failures exit 1; success 0. Complete result before writing; error stdout empty and stderr exact single error line plus LF.

No SQL → REPL, default table; one-shot default CSV; explicit --format overrides either. Prompt always stdout flushed even non-TTY: `minisql> ` empty buffer else `   ...> `. Empty-buffer blank input ignored; stripped dot-prefix line is command. Other lines append joined LF. Execute/clear when right-stripped buffer ends `;`, without SQL-aware completion. Commands .help, .tables, .schema NAME, .format csv|table, .quit/.exit. Unknown command fixed stderr text. Errors continue. EOF executes nonempty buffer then returns 0 with no further output; prompt already emitted before EOF remains.

Sources: contract lines 168–189.

### 5.9 Errors (R21)

Implement every template and position in contract lines 191–205 verbatim. Export MiniSQLError(Exception), LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, QueryRuntimeError, DataIOError; kind Lex/Parse/Semantic/Runtime/IO; message and line/column attributes (both None for IO). SQL string format `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; IO `IOError: <message>`.

Names in errors preserve query spelling without quotes; refs qualified as q.c. Operators keywords and aggregate names uppercase; symbols as written. Duplicate range name at second alias/table name token; call star error at internal star; invalid ESCAPE length at string; division at operator; invalid LIKE at LIKE. EOF at one past last source character, with LF-only position accounting. IO file names basenames. Single-error oracle means no invented tie-break requirements among unrelated competing semantic errors.

## 6. Cost Estimates

No external service/package costs. Primary cost is implementation and contract-edge testing. No optional web expansion needed. Runtime availability risk: default available Python is 3.9.6; installed 3.14 and 3.14-intel64 exit via SIGKILL (-9) before `--version`. Do not install without authorization; test on available runtime with a clearly recorded supported-runtime gap if no working >=3.11 is found. Product must remain Python 3.11+ compatible regardless.

## 7. Task Outline (Preliminary)

1. Foundation: errors, result, tokens, AST/parser and catalog/inference (independent surfaces).
2. Typed binding and execution: static resolution/typing, grouping/order legality, full stage pipeline and operators.
3. Interfaces and integration: API, formatters, CLI/REPL, comprehensive regression and acceptance traceability.

Planning will define non-overlapping task contracts, dependencies, validations and phase gates; each phase requires independent reviewer READY TO ADVANCE and task evidence.

## 8. Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Generic SQL assumptions diverge | Contract-derived tests; no SQL engine oracle |
| Lost source/bare metadata | Retain token and AST spans/parentheses; separate structural keys |
| Lazy/fused execution changes error order | Explicit materialized stage barriers and fault-order tests |
| Incorrect nullable static types | Bind before execute; test empty/unreachable branches |
| Group matching too permissive | Resolved structural keys; no algebraic rewrites |
| CSV newline/physical-line changes | Required open/reader configuration; byte fixtures |
| Cross-platform output drift | Custom quote function, stream reconfigure, golden bytes |
| Host runtime limits | Record exact failed launch evidence and local runtime; do not claim unrun platforms |

### Recorded decisions and alternatives

All decisions are also in mutable `handoff.md`. They resolve underspecified edges only; explicit contract always wins.

- **D1:** Skip all zero-field CSV records, including before header; first nonempty record is header. Alternative: literal first record header. Reason: general skip rule is closest evidence.
- **D2:** NULL is permitted for SUM/AVG as numeric-compatible; SUM(NULL) has NULL static type, AVG(NULL) REAL; both value None. Alternative: reject bare NULL as nonnumeric. Reason: consistent NULL operand acceptance and all-null aggregate outcomes; no defined SUM(NULL) type otherwise.
- **D3:** IN with NULL LHS returns NULL; otherwise evaluate all items left-to-right before deciding membership. Alternative: stop at first match. Reason: only AND/OR explicitly authorize short circuit; avoid hiding failures.
- **D4:** Escape CR/LF in table headers as in cell text. Alternative: retain literal newlines. Reason: headers are cells and aligned table remains deterministic.
- **D5:** Structural keys ignore parentheses/source spelling, compare typed literal value, preserve symbol spelling and operand order; lowercase resolved names. Alternative: source-text keys / normalize comparison synonyms. Reason: same resolved columns/operators/literals, no algebraic extension.
- **D6:** Standard argparse usage diagnostics apply to exit 2; exact single-line engine-error requirement applies to specified query/data errors. Malformed dot-command arguments use unknown-command text. schema unknown table uses SemanticError at 1:1. Unlisted OS read failures become DataIOError with stable basename and OS description where possible. Alternative: invent new templates. Reason: preserve defined behavior; no new public query error template.
- **D7:** No runtime installation; use available tests and report unsupported-runtime/platform execution honestly. Alternative: external installation. Reason: no external-install authority and no need to change product constraints.

No researchers disagreed on an explicit requirement. Unresolved policies and alternatives above are orchestrator decisions, not changes to contract authority.

## 9. Acceptance Criteria

All R1–R21 and AC1–AC12 in `../../contract.md` are mandatory, with a test matrix covering each detailed section. Required anchors include:

- AC1 CLI `SELECT 1 AS one`: bytes `one\n1\n`, exit 0; stdlib import audit.
- AC2 EMP returns 5 rows; missing data exact IO line and exit 3.
- AC3 emp schema INTEGER/TEXT/TEXT/INTEGER.
- AC4 `SELECT 1 # 2`: LexError line 1 column 10.
- AC5 precedence yields 7,-6,1 with exact expression headings.
- AC6 case-insensitive names preserve CSV heading `name`, row Ann.
- AC7 TEXT arithmetic SemanticError at '+' column 13, before execution.
- AC8 integer/real division/remainder and NULL division yield 3,-3,1,3.5,None.
- AC9 NOT IN with NULL yields header only.
- AC10 source heading `salary * 2,n`, row 200,Ann.
- AC11 AVG salary result types [REAL], rows [(95.0,)].
- AC12 all lexical, grammar, type, data, join, aggregate, order, format, protocol and error rules, including edge tests in `research.md`.

Test evidence must include numeric pytest counts, exact commands/runtime, import/compile checks and subprocess byte assertions. A worker PASS alone is insufficient. No acceptance is established by budget checks.

## 10. Dependencies on Prior Features

None. Test dependency pytest only; runtime stdlib. No existing code to preserve. Workflow validators and frozen planning contract apply once planning completes.

## 11. Delegation to Future Specs

No required functionality deferred. Performance optimization, writes, additional SQL, release packaging, external CI platforms and installation are outside this feature. Host-specific test execution gaps are warnings, not silent claims of completion.

2	"""check-dod.py
3	
4	Definition-of-Done checker for a single geeky-implement task. Embodies "verify,
5	don't trust": instead of believing the agent that a task is finished, assert the
6	durable signals on disk before the task may move to Done.
7	
8	Checks for task <ID> in <folder> (missing => ERROR unless noted):
9	  - a per-task notes file tasks/<ID>-*.notes.md exists
10	  - <ID> is placed in the Done lane of kanban.md
11	  - handoff.md mentions <ID>
12	  - WARNING if <ID> still appears in a non-Done lane (In Progress / Blocked / ...)
13	
14	It also extracts and prints the task's "Tests/Validation Before Next Task" block
15	so the orchestrator can re-run those commands itself (this script does not execute
16	them — running is the caller's job, kept framework- and shell-agnostic).
17	
18	Contract: argv in, exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, human summary on stdout.
19	  --json emits a machine-readable object.
20	
21	Usage:
22	  python check-dod.py --path "/abs/docs/feature" --task T3
23	  python check-dod.py "/abs/docs/feature" T3 --json
24	"""
25	
26	from __future__ import annotations
27	
28	import argparse
29	import json
30	import re
31	import sys
32	from pathlib import Path
33	
34	KNOWN_LANES = ("Backlog", "Ready", "In Progress", "In Review", "Blocked", "Done")
35	HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^\s{0,3}#{1,6}\s+(.*\S)\s*$")
36	
37	
38	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
39	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=True)

41	    p.add_argument("--task", dest="task")
42	    p.add_argument("pos_path", nargs="?", default=None)
43	    p.add_argument("pos_task", nargs="?", default=None)
44	    p.add_argument("--json", dest="as_json", action="store_true")
45	    return p.parse_args()
46	
47	
48	def lane_for_heading(heading: str) -> str | None:
49	    norm = heading.strip().lower()
50	    if "validation" in norm:
51	        return None
52	    for lane in KNOWN_LANES:
53	        if norm == lane.lower() or norm.startswith(lane.lower()):
54	            return lane
55	    return None
56	
57	
58	def lanes_for_task(kanban_text: str, task_id: str) -> list[str]:
59	    found: list[str] = []
60	    current: str | None = None
61	    tid_re = re.compile(rf"\b{re.escape(task_id)}\b", re.IGNORECASE)
62	    for line in kanban_text.splitlines():
63	        hm = HEADING_RE.match(line)
64	        if hm:
65	            current = lane_for_heading(hm.group(1))
66	            continue
67	        if current and tid_re.search(line) and current not in found:

90	
91	
92	def main() -> int:

95	    task_id = (args.task or args.pos_task or "").upper()

104	        return 1

106	    errors: list[str] = []
107	    warnings: list[str] = []
108	
109	    # 1. notes file
110	    tasks_dir = folder / "tasks"
111	    notes = []

113	        notes = [f.name for f in tasks_dir.iterdir()
114	                 if f.is_file() and re.match(rf"^{re.escape(task_id)}\b", f.name, re.IGNORECASE)
115	                 and f.name.lower().endswith(".notes.md")]
116	    if not notes:

118	
119	    # 2/4. kanban placement

121	    lanes: list[str] = []

128	        non_done = [l for l in lanes if l != "Done"]

131

44	    p.add_argument("--json", dest="as_json", action="store_true")

47	
48	def lane_for_heading(heading: str) -> str | None:
49	    norm = heading.strip().lower()
50	    if "validation" in norm:
51	        return None
52	    for lane in KNOWN_LANES:
53	        if norm == lane.lower() or norm.startswith(lane.lower()):

55	    return None

58	def lanes_for_task(kanban_text: str, task_id: str) -> list[str]:
59	    found: list[str] = []
60	    current: str | None = None
61	    tid_re = re.compile(rf"\b{re.escape(task_id)}\b", re.IGNORECASE)
