53	
54	Both depend on Done T4; run concurrently with distinct test/product surfaces. T6 tests engine and format/public API, not T5 CLI until integration; T5 owns subprocess CLI/REPL tests. Collect all, run combined full suite/import/compile checks. Independent reviewer returns both task verdicts and phase READY TO ADVANCE, including contract-wide gaps. Done/gates and phase commit. Final stage remains the separately required three-lane impl-review.
55	
56	Dependency edges: T1/T2/T3 → T4 → T5/T6. No cycles. T2/T3 use fixed foundational protocols without completion dependency, enabled by common integration validation and no overlapping writes. Worker scheduling must honor explicit task dependencies; Backlog tasks promoted only after dependencies Done.
57	
58	## Engine design details
59	
60	### Lex / parse
61	
62	Handwritten complete lexer, recursive-descent parser. Positions code points, LF-only lines. Exact ASCII regexes, malformed continuation checks; signs separate. Precedence and non-associative comparison exact. Quoted names/strings decode doubles while retaining original spans. Full tokenize before parse. Parenthesis node/flag preserved for headings/bare ORDER but ignored for structural keys. No FROM yields one empty row.
63	
64	### Semantic
65	
66	Load referenced CSVs in FROM order after parse; no unrelated reads. Scoped ON binding per introduced prefix; aliases hide original qualifiers, duplicate ranges positioned at second range token. Expand wildcards; preserve output headers. Bind resolved column indexes and static types for every expression irrespective of rows, filters, short circuit or pagination. Type operators and conditions exactly, no bool outputs.
67	
68	Discover aggregates in select/HAVING/order; reject forbidden placement/nesting/star. Recursively validate grouping by bound structural keys. Group keys compare column identity, operators, typed literal values, operand order; no text matching/algebraic rewriting. Resolve bare ORDER alias/ordinal before input expression binding; alias wins, duplicate aliases ambiguous. DISTINCT restricts order to selected structure or alias/ordinal. Record projected output indexes for alias/ordinal reuse.
69	
70	### Execute
71	
72	Materialized stage barriers: joins → WHERE → grouping keys/all aggregate arguments → HAVING → select → ORDER keys → first DISTINCT → stable sort → OFFSET/LIMIT. Nested-loop join order and first-seen group order. Global aggregate group exists even empty. Distinct and grouping equate None; normal predicates do not. All aggregate arguments evaluated in input order before HAVING. All projection before order-key evaluation. LIMIT 0 cannot suppress faults.
73	
74	Use explicit 3VL; only AND/OR guaranteed short circuit. NULL arithmetic before zero checks; integer quotient exact truncation (abs quotient/sign), remainder dividend-signed; real math.fmod. LIKE whole-string newline-capable matcher with strict ESCAPE policy. Stable multi-key comparator handles NULL and DESC without reversing tie order. Return complete Result before any CLI writes.
75	
76	### Output / CLI
77	
78	Custom CSV quoting iff prescribed conditions, not csv.writer defaults. Table escapes before measuring, numeric actual values right, NULL left. CLI reconfigure UTF-8/LF only inside main; argparse usage exit 2. Validate data before SQL lexing. One-shot error stdout empty; engine error one stderr line, codes 1/3. REPL prompt/buffer state follows literal textual suffix and EOF rules, .tables/.schema/.format/help/quit/exit, errors continue.
79	
80	## Validation strategy
81	
82	Each task supplies exact pytest commands plus compile checks. `python3` denotes available host interpreter, not a claim that its version satisfies stack target. Record runtime with each suite. Current host default 3.9.6; installed 3.14 variants killed before version output. Product targets >=3.11; maintain compatible stdlib syntax where feasible to enable local checks; do not impose a needless runtime rejection. Seek existing supported interpreter without installation; if unavailable, report as unexecuted-runtime warning and review source compatibility. Windows/Linux byte behavior designed/tested structurally but no unrun OS claimed.
83	
84	Required task suites: lexer/parser, catalog, formatting, semantic, executor, API, CLI, REPL, contract anchors/regressions/import audit. Final `python3 -m pytest -q`, `python3 -m compileall -q minisql`, and stdlib/no sqlite/SQL-engine audit. Exact numeric outcomes and tested revision/content recorded in notes. Tests for all contract sections, not just examples. No external SQL differential oracle.
85	
86	## Review / Done / commit gates
87	
88	Before implementation: validate planning folder, task schema and kanban plus independent plan-review. During work: validate kanban after each lane move. At phase end single independent code-reviewer receives task contracts, worker evidence, concrete changed files and validation commands; returns per-task verdicts and phase READY TO ADVANCE (last phase included). Required fixes coder-owned and reviewed again. Bare claims insufficient; reuse valid revision evidence and rerun invalidated/missing checks.
89	
90	Move approved task to Done provisionally, check-dod and kanban same step; revert from Done on failure. Notes/handoff mandatory. Commit per phase, message lists task IDs and passes check-commit; attribution per session. Never push/force/amend/no-verify. Preserve frozen artifacts throughout implementation. If Blocked, checkpoint notes/kanban/handoff then stop. Final impl-review separately mandatory, fixes preapproved, repeat until overall PASS or budget/capability blocker.
91	
92	## Budget and checkpoint policy
93	
94	Hard deadline 2026-11-04T16:44:18.482771Z; reserve 900s. Research cumulative advisory target 15%, planning 30%, plan-review 40% of usable budget. Planning target 2026-11-04T12:27:48.482771Z. Checkpoint exact incomplete state, never skip gates to claim done.

Reconcile each against ground truth (git status/log, the declared file surface, any `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md`): if the work appears complete, verify saved validation evidence first and run only missing, invalidated, unreliable or explicitly required independent checks, then route it through review → Done normally; if partial or absent, move it back to Ready with a kanban note (`<!-- reset from orphaned in_progress: YYYY-MM-DD -->`).
84	   - If `handoff.md` ends with a `RESUME:` line (see step 17), trust it as the starting hint but verify against kanban (kanban is the source of truth).

86	
87	3. Build an in-memory execution model:
88	   - **Task graph** — node per `Tx-*.md`, edges from each task's `Dependencies:` block.
89	   - **Phase grouping** — derive from `implementation-plan.md` headings if it has explicit phases, else from kanban grouping comments, else by dependency layer (tasks with no unmet deps = layer 0, etc.).
90	   - **File-overlap inference** — for each task, scan its `In scope` / `Module/System` / `Technical Notes` for filenames, modules, or package paths. Two tasks are file-conflicting if their declared surfaces overlap.
91	   - **Eligibility** — task is eligible iff it sits in kanban Ready AND every dependency is Done, or is In Review in the current phase with passing validation evidence.
92	
93	4. If `--dry-run` is set, print the execution model (phase order, per-phase batches, parallel groups with justifications) and STOP. Otherwise continue.
94	
95	### Phase 1 — Execute each phase
96	
97	For each phase, in plan order:
98	
99	5. **Select the next batch** of eligible tasks. Before dispatch and at every phase boundary, consume optional `GEEKY_DEADLINE_UTC` (UTC timestamp) and `GEEKY_CLOSEOUT_RESERVE_S` (nonnegative seconds within the hard budget). When both are absent, continue normally. With context present, calculate remaining time; within the advisory reserve prioritize required acceptance and closeout over optional work. If insufficient time remains for required work, save exact incomplete task/review state, evidence and next command in notes/handoff, pause the heartbeat and stop dispatching. Invalid context must be reported and checkpointed, never treated as extra allowance. Deadline or reserve expiry never establishes acceptance, moves an unmet task to Done, or substitutes for a required reviewer/gate. Batch size = min(3, eligible count, parallelism flag). A batch is parallel-safe iff:
100	   - no task in the batch depends on another task in the batch, AND
101	   - no two tasks in the batch have overlapping declared file surfaces, AND
102	   - none of them is marked P0-blocker-for-others in the implementation plan.
103	   Otherwise reduce batch size or fall back to serial. Record the justification in the per-task notes file (step 10).
104	
105	6. **Move every task in the batch from Ready to In Progress** in `kanban.md`. Add a timestamp comment beside each: `<!-- in_progress: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM -->`. Refresh `.heartbeat` (`ts` = now, `task` = batch's first task ID, `status` = `running`).
106	
107	7. **Delegate implementation to `geeky-coder`.** When the batch has >1 task, send a SINGLE message with multiple `Agent` tool calls in parallel (this is required — do not serialize parallel work into separate messages). Each brief must be self-contained:
108	   - Full text of the task file (paste it — coders don't share your context).
109	   - **Verified absolute paths** for every file/folder the brief references — verify each exists (Glob/ls) before writing the brief; never pass an assumed path. Subagents don't share your context or memory, and assumed paths are a top wasted-turn cause.
110	   - Pointers to relevant sections of `implementation-plan.md` and `feature-specification.md` by heading + line range, not just filename.
111	   - Acceptance criteria copied verbatim.
112	   - The validation block from the task file (`Tests/Validation Before Next Task`). Resolve uncertain prerequisites with the smallest useful check before committing to broader work. Reuse established methods and valid evidence. Preserve required ordering and acceptance gates; an early diagnostic result does not replace them.
113	   - Explicit instruction: *do not modify files outside the declared In Scope surface; if you discover the scope is wrong, stop and report — do not silently expand.*
114	   - Give the worker authority to finish the bounded assignment, including compatible fixes and required checks. Ask for a consolidated return; interrupt only for blockers, scope decisions or ownership conflicts, not each small edit. Contact the worker only for new information, a blocker, a decision or a completed result; use completion waits instead of repeated status requests. User progress updates do not require another worker round trip.
115	   - Use the harness's actual dispatch schema and callable role name. Apply the canonical-instructions fallback above only when needed; record the substitution once.
116	   - The absolute path of `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md`, where the worker writes its detail, and a return limit of ~15 lines (see Main-thread budget).
117	
118	8. **Verify the task's validation evidence** after each coder returns. Require the tested revision or file hashes, exact commands, exit status and results. Inspect the saved output through a tail; a bare claim of PASS is insufficient. Reuse passing evidence for unchanged code, dependencies and relevant environment. Execute missing checks or rerun only when evidence is invalidated, unreliable, or independent execution is explicitly required. Before repeating a test or review, record what changed or remains unproved, which evidence is invalidated, and the smallest check that resolves it. Reuse valid evidence unless a required check is missing or independent execution is explicitly mandated. If a required command fails:
119	   - Capture the failure output.
120	   - Re-delegate to `geeky-coder` once with the failure context for a fix attempt.
121	   - If it still fails, move the task to **Blocked** with a kanban note that includes the validation command and the failure summary, finalize state per the Constitution, and return to the user.
122	
123	9. **Move the task from In Progress to In Review** once its validation evidence passes. It waits there for the phase review (step 14); do not dispatch a per-task review. Its dependents in this phase may start now (step 3 eligibility).
124	
125	10. **Write a per-task notes file** `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md` (creating it if the worker has not, NOT editing the original task file) containing:
126	    - Parallelization decision and justification.
127	    - Coder summary (one paragraph).
128	    - Validation results (command + pass/fail).
129	    - Review findings, grouped by severity.
130	    - Resolution: which findings were fixed in this run vs deferred (with rationale).
131	    - Final diff scope (list of touched files).
132	    Keep review scope, any reopened evidence and the next action in these existing notes. Do not create another ledger or approval gate.
133	
134	11. **Resolve findings:** send blocking findings from the phase review to `geeky-coder`, batching compatible in-scope fixes into one assignment per owner. Respect dependencies and shared files; do not dispatch one correction at a time when they can be fixed together. Rerun affected checks; dependents of a changed task re-run their validation. Re-review only the affected tasks, in one dispatch, against the changed scope plus the original findings. Preserve unaffected evidence. Blockers and majors within the review contract must be resolved before Done; record unrelated findings separately. Log deferred minors and nits in `handoff.md`.
135	
136	Acceptance must wait until all required tests have passing evidence, even when the task is not in the Blocked lane. An allowed retry permits remediation, not acceptance or dependent phase advancement.
137	
138	12. **Move to Done** in `kanban.md` only after the phase review clears (steps 14–15): validation is green AND the task has a PASS verdict AND no blocker/major findings remain. The **Definition-of-Done** gate verifies the task in the Done lane, so run it in the same step as the Done move, followed by the **kanban-integrity** gate. If `check-dod` does not exit 0, move the task back and fix before trying again; never leave a task in Done with a failing gate. Fix until both exit 0:
139	
140	    ```
141	    python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check-dod.py" --path "<folder>" --task T<x>
142	    python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-kanban.py" --path "<folder>"
143	    ```
144	
145	    `check-dod` also prints the task's validation block. Match it to the verified evidence from step 8; printing the commands does not require another execution. Run `validate-kanban` after every lane move, not only at Done, so the board never drifts from truth. Refresh `.heartbeat` on the Done move. If either gate CRASHES (traceback / missing module rather than a clean non-zero): say so in one line, run the equivalent manual check (read the DoD block and verify each item; eyeball lane membership), record the crash in the per-task notes, and continue VISIBLY — a crashed gate must never become a silent stall.
146	
147	13. **Repeat steps 5–10** until the current phase has no eligible Ready tasks left, then go to step 14. Steps 11–12 run on the phase review's findings and verdicts.
148	
149	### Phase 2 — End of phase: phase review + commits
150	
151	14. **Phase review** at the end of every phase, including the last; `impl-review` does not replace it. Dispatch ONE `geeky-orchestration:code-reviewer` subagent that reviews every task in the phase and issues the phase verdict. If the phase has more than 4 tasks, or its diff is too large to review AC by AC in one pass, split it into dispatches of at most 4 related tasks; the last dispatch issues the phase verdict using the others' task verdicts as inputs. The **READY TO ADVANCE** or **BLOCKED** verdict must come from that subagent, never from the orchestrator; record its agent ID in the step-17 `handoff.md` phase block. Brief it with:
152	    - Phase name and the phase's task IDs (In Review, plus any already Done).
153	    - For each task: the task template, ACs and validation evidence.
154	    - The aggregated diff for the phase (`git diff` from the phase's starting commit to HEAD).
155	    - The per-task notes files for the phase.
156	    - The relevant section of `implementation-plan.md`.
157	
158	    **Task verdicts** — one per task, kept separate:
159	    - The decision is: **Does this task meet every AC and pass its defined tests?** Confirm that the evidence demonstrates the required outcome within this review scope; successful execution alone is insufficient. Return an AC-by-AC result, test result and PASS or NEEDS FIXES. Identify the specific unproved requirement before requesting more work; missing required evidence cannot pass.
160	    - Inspect immediate dependencies only as needed to answer that question. Do not review the entire implementation chain or add acceptance requirements. Route unrelated findings separately; block a task only when a finding prevents its contract from being met or makes acceptance unsafe under an existing requirement.
161	    - Every blocking finding must cite the violated AC, defined test or existing mandatory constraint, concrete evidence, and the smallest necessary correction. Severity alone does not authorize extra scope. Record optional improvements as follow-ups.
162	    - Return one complete finding set per task, grouped by severity.
163	
164	    **Phase verdict** — review the complete phase requirements, combined behavior, cross-task interactions, shared contracts and phase-level validation, using the task verdicts as inputs. Answer explicitly: **Can we move to the next phase?** Return **READY TO ADVANCE** or **BLOCKED**, with evidence for requirement coverage and any unmet requirement or dependency. All phase tasks must be accounted for; an unfinished required task cannot pass this gate.
165	
166	15. **Integrate phase findings** using step 11. Resolve failures within the approved scope; the re-review dispatch covers only the affected tasks and returns an updated verdict for that same phase before Done. An earlier phase's READY verdict cannot clear a later BLOCKED phase. Do not repeat task reviews without changed code or dependencies, contradictory evidence or a concrete defect affecting the phase. Do not start the next phase until **READY TO ADVANCE** is recorded in the step-17 `handoff.md` phase block. If a blocker cannot be resolved under the existing task contracts, mark Blocked and return with the exact unmet requirement. Minors that do not prevent advancement remain deferred. Then move each cleared task to Done (step 12) before committing.
167	
168	16. **Commit the phase diff, split into multiple small logically-grouped commits.** Decide grouping by reading the diff yourself; each functional delivery includes its required code and tests. Before accepting a committed task snapshot, compare its code, tests and relevant dependencies with the tested revision/file hashes from step 8. Matching inputs and relevant environment permit evidence reuse; missing tests or mismatched inputs require affected validation in an isolated tree at that snapshot. A later final-HEAD pass cannot justify an earlier snapshot. Preserve existing task/Done commit selection (H1); do not rewrite anchors to obtain a pass. Save full commit IDs, exact commands, exit codes and results in the task notes. Each commit message format:
169	
170	    ```
171	    feat(<phase-short-name>): <what this commit changes>
172	
173	    Tasks: T<x>
174	    Refs: docs/<planning-folder>/tasks/Tx-*.md
175	    ```
176	
177	    Name several tasks on the `Tasks:` line only when their changes form one concern.
178	
179	    Use HEREDOC to pass multiline messages. Do NOT push. Do NOT amend. If a pre-commit hook fails, have `geeky-coder` fix any product code or test cause, then create a NEW commit — do not skip hooks.
180	
181	    Before each commit, validate the message with the **commit gate** (`--message` works in PowerShell and bash; in bash you may pipe the message via stdin instead). A non-zero exit blocks that commit: fix the message and re-run the gate until it exits 0, then commit.
182	
183	    Make each commit a checked step of its own. If the gate or `git commit` fails, stop there: do not stage files for the next commit until this one exists, because the next `git add` would sweep the staged files into it. Before staging the next commit, confirm the previous one landed (`git log -1`) and nothing is left staged (`git diff --cached --quiet`).
184	
185	    ```
186	    python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check-commit.py" --message "<msg>"
187	    printf '%s' "$msg" | python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check-commit.py"   # bash alternative
188	    ```
189	
190	17. **Update `handoff.md`** with a phase summary block:
191	    - Phase name, date, duration.
192	    - Tasks completed, tasks blocked (if any).
193	    - Commits created (short SHAs).
194	    - Phase review verdict, reviewer agent ID, supporting evidence and any advancement blockers.
195	    - Deferred follow-ups added in this phase.
196	    - End with a single checkpoint line so any future session can resume with zero re-prompting: `RESUME: <next phase or "run complete"> — next eligible: <task IDs or none>`. Replace the previous `RESUME:` line each time (it is a cursor, not a log).
197	
198	### Phase 3 — End of run
199	
200	18. When all phases complete (or backlog is empty, or a task is blocked):
201	    - When all phases are accepted, route final implementation review to [impl-review](../../impl-review/SKILL.md). Invoke it when final review is authorized by the request or standing workflow; otherwise record it as the next step. Do not substitute another final review or claim final acceptance before its verdict. A phase-only run does not trigger package-wide review.
202	    - Once the authorized gates pass, finish required closeout and report completion. Do not add discretionary hardening, broader tests or another review. Reopen only for evidence of an unmet approved requirement or mandatory constraint; record optional work as a follow-up.
203	    - Append a "Run Summary" section to `handoff.md` with: total tasks completed, total commits, blocked items, deferred follow-ups, suggested next-session start steps.
204	    - Reconcile `kanban.md` lanes and counts with task evidence and the original task count; record current required task, phase and authorized final-review verdicts. An incomplete review or interrupted closeout remains incomplete.
205	    - Only then set `.heartbeat` `status` to `done` if required work and closeout are complete; otherwise set `paused` with a truthful resume block, including interrupted or Blocked state.
206	    - Print to the user: a short status (Done count, Blocked count, Deferred count) and the path to the updated handoff. Suggest the `geeky-status` skill (`/geeky-status <folder>`) as the lightweight follow-up.
207	    - State review and gate claims only as recorded in `handoff.md`, citing reviewer agent IDs. Check each final claim against its source and reviewed scope: distinguish direct function-call coverage from subprocess/CLI coverage, and Git object IDs from file SHA-256 digests. Missing one coverage form does not mean all coverage is absent. List any skipped or self-issued gate under Deviations.
208	
209	## Parallelization rules
210	
211	When deciding whether to parallelize a batch, apply this checklist explicitly and write the result to the per-task notes file:
212	
213	| Check | Pass condition |
214	|---|---|
215	| Declared dependencies | No task in batch depends on another task in batch (transitively) |
216	| File-surface overlap | Pairwise intersection of declared In Scope files/modules is empty |
217	| Shared mutable artifacts | None of the tasks edit the same migration, lockfile, or generated bundle |
218	| Coordination cost | Tasks are conceptually independent — a reviewer can review them without needing to read the other |
219	| Resource ceiling | Total concurrent coders ≤ 3 (or 1 if `--serial`) |
220	
221	If any check fails for a candidate pair, demote to serial for that pair.
222	
223	Task reviews run together inside the phase review, on stable diffs. Tests or reviewer probes that mutate the same database, fixtures, ports or files must be isolated or serialized.
224	
225	Batch independent reads and compatible checks in one dispatch. A shared validation run may satisfy several tasks only when its command, configuration and tested revision meet each task's contract; retain a result for every task. Collect independent failures before remediation when safe. Stop dependent or destructive checks on failure. Separate product defects from harness and environment faults, then fix each compatible set together. Reserve broad final gates for a stable candidate unless the plan explicitly requires them earlier.
226	
227	## Failure modes
228	
229	After two unsuccessful correction cycles on the same issue, diagnose the cause before repeating the approach: product defect, test expectation, harness/fixture, environment, or unresolved requirement. Record the cause and bounded next action in existing notes. This does not grant extra retries or waive a failed gate; any earlier stop condition still applies.
230	
231	These are recoverable — handle inline, do not stop the run:
232	- Coder reports a typo or import error → re-delegate once with the error log.
233	- Pre-commit hook fails on whitespace/lint → route the fix to `geeky-coder` and create a new commit.
234	- Code-review surfaces minor/nit findings → log under Deferred, proceed.
235	- A gate/validator script CRASHES (traceback, missing module) → one-line surface, manual check of the same criteria, note it, continue; flag the plugin for a fix at run end. Never a silent stall.
236	- 401/auth-expiry symptoms mid-run → FIRST append a resume block to `handoff.md` (current task, exact state, next command) and set `.heartbeat` to `paused`; the session may be unrecoverable and the handoff is what survives.
237	- API-error interruption (`<synthetic>` model turn in the log = the API cut the turn off, no auto-resume; external, not your fault) → FIRST checkpoint (`handoff.md` + `.heartbeat` `paused`), then resume — the fix depends on the subtype, so read the turn's text:
238	  - **spend/usage limit** ("hit your monthly spend limit") → raise it at claude.ai/settings/usage or wait; a `/model` switch does NOT help (account-level quota).
239	  - **session limit** ("hit your session limit — resets …") → wait for the reset; `/model` does not help.
240	  - **401 / auth** ("run /login") → re-auth; the session may be unrecoverable, so the handoff is what survives.
241	  - **529 / overloaded** (genuine capacity) → `/model` switch (capacity is per-model) or wait; status.claude.com. Upstream: anthropics/claude-code #60577, #35801.
242	
243	**Diagnosing a quiet/stalled run** — when a run has gone silent, check causes in THIS order (cheapest first; the first is external, not model quality):
244	1. **API-error interruption** — scan the session log tail for `<synthetic>` model turns (NOT for the string "529" — in this environment the real population is spend-limit / session-limit / 401; a genuine 529/overload has not actually occurred here). Fix per subtype above.
245	2. **Validator/gate crash** — a gate scripted itself into a traceback and the loop absorbed it.
246	3. **Logic/plan problem** — only after ruling out the external causes above. Misattributing an external interruption to "the model got stuck" wastes a wrong-fix cycle.
247	
248	These STOP the run (mark Blocked, update handoff, return to user):
249	- A task's validation block fails after one retry.
250	- Code review surfaces a blocker that the coder cannot fix in one follow-up.
251	- Phase review remains BLOCKED after bounded remediation, or requires a change to the approved task contracts.
252	- A task's declared scope is materially wrong (file doesn't exist, dependency missing from plan).
253	- Any merge conflict between parallel coders (this means the parallelization decision was wrong — record the lesson in the notes file).
254	
255	## Acceptance criteria
256	
257	A successful run leaves the folder in this state:
258	
259	1. `kanban.md` reflects current truth — every task is in exactly one lane, Done tasks have `[x]`, In Progress / Blocked tasks carry a timestamp comment.
260	2. `handoff.md` has a new "Run Summary" section at the bottom plus per-phase entries.
261	3. `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md` exists for every task touched in this run.
262	4. The project tree has commits (none pushed) that map cleanly to the phases executed.
263	5. No edits to `implementation-plan.md`, `feature-specification.md`, `draft.md`, `references.md`, or original `tasks/Tx-*.md` files.
264	6. If anything was blocked, the user sees a clear "Blocked: T<x> — <reason>" line and knows where to look.
265	7. `.heartbeat` is finalized (`done`, or `paused` with a matching resume block in `handoff.md`) — never left as a stale `running`.
266	
267	A `--dry-run` invocation must produce the execution model output and modify nothing.
268	
269	"}]}]

33	
34	## Language reference
35	
36	### Lexical rules
37	
38	- Whitespace: space, tab, `\r`, `\n`. Comments: `--` to end of line.
39	- Lines split on `\n` only; line and column are 1-based; column counts code points; tab and `\r` count as one column.
40	- Keywords (reserved, case-insensitive): `SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN`.
41	- Unquoted identifier: `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, not a keyword. Quoted identifier: `"..."` with `""` for a literal `"`; may contain any character and may equal a keyword. Function names (`COUNT SUM AVG MIN MAX`) are ordinary identifiers.
42	- String literal: `'...'` with `''` for a literal `'`; may span lines; no backslash escapes (`\` is literal).
43	- INTEGER literal: `[0-9]+`. REAL literal: `[0-9]+\.[0-9]*([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, `\.[0-9]+([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, or `[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`. A numeric literal immediately followed by a letter, digit, `_` or `.` is a LexError (`invalid number literal`). Signs are unary operators.
44	- Operators: `+ - * / % = <> != < <= > >= ( ) , . * ;`.
45	
46	### Grammar (EBNF)
47	
48	```
49	query     = "SELECT" ["DISTINCT"] item {"," item}
50	            ["FROM" tableref {join}] ["WHERE" expr]
51	            ["GROUP" "BY" expr {"," expr}] ["HAVING" expr]
52	            ["ORDER" "BY" order {"," order}]
53	            ["LIMIT" INT] ["OFFSET" INT] [";"] EOF ;
54	item      = "*" | name "." "*" | expr [["AS"] name] ;
55	tableref  = name [["AS"] name] ;
56	join      = (["INNER"] "JOIN" | "LEFT" ["OUTER"] "JOIN") tableref "ON" expr ;
57	order     = expr ["ASC" | "DESC"] ;
58	expr      = and {"OR" and} ;
59	and       = not {"AND" not} ;
60	not       = "NOT" not | cmp ;
61	cmp       = add [ cmpop add | "IS" ["NOT"] "NULL"
62	                | ["NOT"] "LIKE" add ["ESCAPE" STRING]
63	                | ["NOT"] "IN" "(" expr {"," expr} ")" ] ;
64	cmpop     = "=" | "<>" | "!=" | "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=" ;
65	add       = mul {("+" | "-") mul} ;
66	mul       = unary {("*" | "/" | "%") unary} ;
67	unary     = ("-" | "+") unary | primary ;
68	primary   = INT | REAL | STRING | "NULL" | call | colref | "(" expr ")" ;
69	call      = name "(" ("*" | expr) ")" ;
70	colref    = name ["." name] ;
71	name      = IDENT | QUOTED_IDENT ;
72	```
73	
74	`FROM` is optional; without it the query runs over exactly one empty row. A table alias makes the table name unusable as a qualifier in that query.
75	
76	### Precedence (highest first)
77	
78	| Level | Operators | Associativity |
79	|---|---|---|
80	| 1 | unary `-`, `+` | right |
81	| 2 | `*` `/` `%` | left |
82	| 3 | binary `+` `-` | left |
83	| 4 | `= <> != < <= > >=`, `IS [NOT] NULL`, `[NOT] LIKE`, `[NOT] IN` | none (`a = b = c` is a ParseError at the second operator) |
84	| 5 | `NOT` | right |
85	| 6 | `AND` | left |
86	| 7 | `OR` | left |
87	
88	### Types and values
89	
90	- Static types: `INTEGER` (`int`), `REAL` (`float`), `TEXT` (`str`), `NULL` (bare `NULL` literal only). Any value may be `None`; never `bool`. Comparison, logical, `IS`, `LIKE`, `IN` yield INTEGER `1`, `0` or NULL.
91	- Arithmetic operands must be INTEGER, REAL or NULL type. Result type: REAL if either operand is REAL; else NULL if both are NULL; else INTEGER. Unary minus/plus keeps its operand type.
92	- Comparisons (`=`, `<>`, `IN` items, `MIN`/`MAX`, ordering) require both sides numeric (INTEGER/REAL mixed freely, compared numerically) or both TEXT, or either side NULL type. TEXT compares by Python `str` ordering (code points, case-sensitive).
93	- `LIKE` operands and `ESCAPE` must be TEXT or NULL. `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` operands and `WHERE`/`ON`/`HAVING` conditions must be INTEGER, REAL or NULL type; nonzero is true, zero is false, NULL is unknown.
94	- Integer `/` truncates toward zero (`-7 / 2` = `-3`); integer `%` takes the sign of the dividend (`-7 % 2` = `-1`, `7 % -2` = `1`). REAL `/` is float division; REAL `%` is `math.fmod`.
95	- If either arithmetic operand is NULL the result is NULL (checked first). Otherwise a zero divisor for `/` or `%` (INTEGER or REAL) raises RuntimeError `division by zero` at the operator.
96	
97	### NULL and predicates
98	
99	- Any comparison with a NULL operand is NULL. `NOT NULL` is NULL. `AND`: false if either side false, else NULL if either NULL, else true. `OR`: true if either true, else NULL if either NULL, else false.
100	- `x IS NULL` / `x IS NOT NULL` return 1/0, never NULL.
101	- `x [NOT] IN (list)`: NULL if `x` is NULL; 1 if some item equals `x`; else NULL if any item is NULL; else 0. `NOT IN` negates with 3VL.
102	- `LIKE`: whole-string, case-sensitive; `%` matches any sequence (including empty), `_` exactly one character. With `ESCAPE 'c'`, `c` followed by `%`, `_` or `c` matches that character literally; `c` followed by anything else or at pattern end raises RuntimeError `invalid LIKE pattern` at the `LIKE` token. `ESCAPE` must be a one-character string literal. Any NULL operand gives NULL.
103	- Equality for `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT` treats NULL as equal to NULL; join conditions follow normal 3VL, so NULL never matches.
104	
105	### Type inference
106	
107	For each column, over its non-empty raw fields (no trimming): if every field fully matches `[+-]?[0-9]+` the column is INTEGER (`int(field)`); else if every field fully matches `[+-]?([0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+|[0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` it is REAL (`float(field)`); else TEXT (fields kept verbatim, including numeric-looking ones). A column with no non-empty fields is TEXT. Empty fields (quoted or not) are NULL in every type. Consequently `" 1"` makes a column TEXT, `007` is INTEGER `7`, and `1`, `2.5` makes a REAL column.
108	
109	## Interface contract
110	
111	### Data directory
112	
113	- `--data DIR` (default `.`); library `connect(DIR)`. A missing or non-directory `DIR` is an IOError: `connect(DIR)` raises `DataIOError` immediately, and the one-shot CLI reports it and exits 3 before lexing the SQL.
114	- A table is any regular file directly in `DIR` whose name ends in `.csv` (case-insensitive). Table name = file stem; lookup is case-insensitive. Two files whose stems are equal case-insensitively make every reference to that name an IOError `ambiguous table file '<name>'`.
115	- Files are read on each `execute` with `encoding='utf-8-sig'`, `newline=''` and `csv.reader(f, strict=True)` (default dialect). Only the tables referenced in `FROM`/`JOIN` are read; any other file in `DIR`, however malformed, never affects a query. `tables()` lists stems without reading file contents.
116	- Row 1 is the header; names are used verbatim. Empty header name, or duplicate names (case-insensitive), is an IOError. Lines yielding zero fields are skipped. A record with a different field count than the header is IOError `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M`, where N is the reader's `line_num` after that record.
117	
118	### Name resolution and output names
119	
120	- Column reference `c` searches all tables in `FROM`; `q.c` searches the table whose range name (alias, else table name) is `q`. Zero matches: unknown column; more than one: ambiguous column. Duplicate range names are a SemanticError. An `ON` condition sees only tables introduced before or in its own join; later tables are unknown there. Joins associate left.
121	- `*` expands to all columns of all tables in `FROM` order; `t.*` to that table's columns. Duplicate output names are allowed.
122	- Output name: the alias as written (quotes removed); else for an unparenthesized column reference, the column's header name as in the CSV; else the verbatim source text of the item from its first to last character (e.g. `COUNT(*)`, `a + 1`, `(a)`).
123	
124	### Aggregates and grouping
125	
126	- A query is an aggregate query if it has `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, or an aggregate call in the select list or `ORDER BY`.
127	- `COUNT(*)` counts rows; `COUNT(e)` counts non-NULL values (INTEGER). `SUM` of INTEGER is INTEGER, of REAL is REAL. `AVG` is REAL. `MIN`/`MAX` keep the argument type. All ignore NULLs. Over zero non-NULL values `COUNT` is `0`, others NULL. `SUM`/`AVG` need numeric arguments; only `COUNT` accepts `*`.
128	- Without `GROUP BY` the whole filtered input (after `WHERE`) forms a single group, even when empty; without `HAVING` the query yields exactly one row, and `HAVING` filters that group, yielding 0 or 1 row (1 row over empty input when `HAVING` is true, e.g. `HAVING COUNT(*) = 0`). With `GROUP BY`, empty input yields zero rows; groups appear in first-seen order unless ordered.
129	- In an aggregate query, every select, `HAVING` and `ORDER BY` expression must be built from aggregate calls, literals, and subexpressions structurally identical to a `GROUP BY` expression (same resolved columns, operators and literals). `*` is not allowed. Aggregates are not allowed in `WHERE`, `ON`, `GROUP BY`, or inside another aggregate.
130	
131	### ORDER BY, DISTINCT, LIMIT
132	
133	- An `ORDER BY` item that is a bare INTEGER literal is a 1-based output ordinal, counted after `*` expansion. A bare identifier equal to exactly one select-item alias (written with or without `AS`) refers to that output column (two such aliases: ambiguous column). Otherwise it is an expression over input rows (or groups).
134	- With `DISTINCT`, each `ORDER BY` item must be an ordinal, an alias, or structurally identical to a select expression.
135	- Sorting is stable; ties keep pre-sort order for both `ASC` and `DESC`. NULL sorts before every value (first in `ASC`, last in `DESC`).
136	- `LIMIT 0` yields no rows; `OFFSET` past the end yields no rows.
137	
138	### Evaluation order
139	
140	1. `FROM`/joins: nested loop; for each left row in order, right rows in file order; `ON` evaluated for every pair; `LEFT JOIN` emits one NULL-filled row for an unmatched left row.
141	2. `WHERE` per row. 3. Group keys and aggregate arguments per surviving row. 4. `HAVING` per group. 5. Select expressions per surviving row/group. 6. `ORDER BY` keys. 7. `DISTINCT` (first occurrence kept). 8. Sort. 9. `OFFSET`, then `LIMIT`.
142	
143	`AND` skips its right side when the left is false; `OR` when the left is true. Rows are processed in order within each step; the first failure is reported and no output is produced.
144	
145	### Library API
146	
147	```python
148	minisql.connect(data_dir: str | os.PathLike) -> Connection
149	Connection.execute(sql: str) -> Result
150	Connection.tables() -> list[str]                    # stems, sorted by (lower(), name)
151	Connection.schema(table: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]  # (column, type) in header order
152	@dataclass(frozen=True)
153	class Result: columns: list[str]; types: list[str]; rows: list[tuple]
154	minisql.format_csv(result: Result) -> str
155	minisql.format_table(result: Result) -> str
156	```
157	
158	`types` holds `"INTEGER"`, `"REAL"`, `"TEXT"` or `"NULL"`. Row values are `int`, `float`, `str` or `None`.
159	
160	### Output formats
161	
162	Value text: INTEGER `str(v)`; REAL `repr(v)` (`100.0`, `2.5`, `1e+20`); TEXT verbatim.
163	
164	**CSV** (`--format csv`, default for one-shot): header line, then one line per row, fields joined by `,`, every line terminated by `\n` (also on Windows). NULL is an empty unquoted field. A field is wrapped in `"` (inner `"` doubled) iff it is the empty string, contains `,`, `"`, `\n` or `\r`, or starts or ends with a space. Header names follow the same quoting.
165	
166	**Table** (`--format table`, default for REPL): cell text is the value text with newline and carriage-return characters replaced by the two-character escapes `\n` and `\r`; NULL is `NULL`. Width of a column = max code-point length of header and cells. Header cells left-aligned; INTEGER/REAL values right-aligned; TEXT and `NULL` left-aligned. Cells joined by ` | `; separator line is `-` × width per column joined by `-+-`; trailing spaces stripped from every line; then `(N rows)` or `(1 row)`. Every line ends with `\n`.
167	
168	### CLI
169	
170	`python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]`. With `SQL`: one-shot, print the formatted result to stdout. Without `SQL`: REPL on stdin. stdout and stderr are UTF-8 with `\n`.
171	
172	### REPL
173	
174	- Prompt `minisql> ` when the buffer is empty, `   ...> ` otherwise; written to stdout without newline, flushed, whether or not stdin is a TTY. Input is not echoed.
175	- With an empty buffer, a line whose stripped text starts with `.` is a command; a blank line is ignored. Otherwise the line is appended (joined with `\n`); when the buffer, right-stripped, ends with `;`, it is executed and cleared.
176	- Commands: `.help` (free text), `.tables` (one name per line, `tables()` order), `.schema NAME` (`name TYPE` per line), `.format csv|table`, `.quit` and `.exit`. Unknown command: stderr `unknown command: <text>`.
177	- Results print in the current format (CSV has no row-count footer). Errors print one line to stderr and the session continues; positions are relative to the buffer.
178	- At EOF a non-empty buffer is executed; then exit 0 with nothing further printed. `.quit` exits 0.
179	
180	### Exit codes (one-shot)
181	
182	| Code | Meaning |
183	|---|---|
184	| 0 | success |
185	| 1 | LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, RuntimeError |
186	| 2 | usage error (argparse) |
187	| 3 | IOError |
188	
189	On error stdout is empty and stderr holds exactly the error line plus `\n`. No tracebacks.

191	## Error handling
192	
193	Classes exported from `minisql`, subclassing `MiniSQLError(Exception)`: `LexError`, `ParseError`, `SemanticError`, `QueryRuntimeError`, `DataIOError`, with attributes `kind` (`Lex`/`Parse`/`Semantic`/`Runtime`/`IO`), `line`, `column` (`None` for IO), `message`; `str(err)` is the formatted line.
194	
195	Format: `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; IO errors: `IOError: <message>`.
196	
197	| Kind | Message templates | Position |
198	|---|---|---|
199	| Lex | `unexpected character 'X'`, `unterminated string literal`, `unterminated quoted identifier`, `invalid number literal` | offending character / opening quote / literal start |
200	| Parse | `unexpected token 'T'` (T = token source text), `unexpected end of input` | token start / one past last input character |
201	| Semantic | `unknown table 'N'`, `duplicate table name 'N'`, `unknown column 'R'`, `ambiguous column 'R'`, `unknown function 'F'`, `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT`, `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T1 and T2`, `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T`, `condition must be numeric, got TEXT`, `aggregate function not allowed here`, `column 'R' must appear in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate`, `'*' not allowed in aggregate query`, `ORDER BY position N is out of range`, `ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used`, `ESCAPE must be a single character` | table/name token; column ref start; operator token (function name for aggregates); condition/expression start; `*`; ordinal; ESCAPE string |
202	| Runtime | `division by zero`, `invalid LIKE pattern` | `/` or `%` token; `LIKE` token |
203	| IO | `data directory not found: DIR` (DIR as given), `ambiguous table file 'N'`, `<file>: empty file`, `<file>: empty column name`, `<file>: duplicate column 'C'`, `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M`, `<file>: line N: malformed CSV`, `<file>: invalid UTF-8` | none |
204	
205	`N`, `R`, `F` are names as written in the query without quotes (`R` qualified as `q.c`). `OP` is the operator as written for symbols, upper-case for keywords and aggregates (`LIKE`, `IN`, `AND`, `SUM`). `<file>` is the base file name. For `duplicate table name 'N'`, the position is the range-name token of the second `tableref` with that range name (its alias if present, else its table name) and `N` is that range name as written. For `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT`, the position is the `*` token inside the call. For `duplicate column 'C'`, `C` is the second occurrence's header name exactly as written in the CSV. For `malformed CSV`, `N` is the reader's `line_num` at the moment `csv.Error` is raised. Phases run lex → parse → semantic (including IO for referenced tables, in `FROM` order) → execute. The oracle only uses queries containing a single error.

58	## Engine design details
59	
60	### Lex / parse
61	
62	Handwritten complete lexer, recursive-descent parser. Positions code points, LF-only lines. Exact ASCII regexes, malformed continuation checks; signs separate. Precedence and non-associative comparison exact. Quoted names/strings decode doubles while retaining original spans. Full tokenize before parse. Parenthesis node/flag preserved for headings/bare ORDER but ignored for structural keys. No FROM yields one empty row.
63	
64	### Semantic
65	
66	Load referenced CSVs in FROM order after parse; no unrelated reads. Scoped ON binding per introduced prefix; aliases hide original qualifiers, duplicate ranges positioned at second range token. Expand wildcards; preserve output headers. Bind resolved column indexes and static types for every expression irrespective of rows, filters, short circuit or pagination. Type operators and conditions exactly, no bool outputs.
67	
68	Discover aggregates in select/HAVING/order; reject forbidden placement/nesting/star. Recursively validate grouping by bound structural keys. Group keys compare column identity, operators, typed literal values, operand order; no text matching/algebraic rewriting. "1	"""Command-line transport and the literal, line-buffered interactive protocol."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import argparse
6	import sys
7	
8	from . import Connection, DataIOError, MiniSQLError, connect, format_csv, format_table
9	
10	
11	_HELP = """Commands:
12	  .help              Show this help
13	  .tables            List tables
14	  .schema NAME       Show column names and types
15	  .format csv|table  Change result format
16	  .quit / .exit      Exit
17	Enter SQL ending in a semicolon; unfinished SQL runs at EOF.
18	"""
19	
20	
21	def _report_error(error: MiniSQLError) -> None:
22	    sys.stderr.write(f"{error}\n")
23	
24	
25	def _execute(connection: Connection, sql: str, output_format: str) -> None:
26	    formatter = format_csv if output_format == "csv" else format_table
27	    text = formatter(connection.execute(sql))
28	    sys.stdout.write(text)
29	
30	
31	def _repl(connection: Connection, output_format: str) -> int:
32	    buffer = []
33	    while True:
34	        sys.stdout.write("   ...> " if buffer else "minisql> ")
35	        sys.stdout.flush()
36	        line = sys.stdin.readline()
37	        eof = line == ""
38	        try:
39	            if eof:
40	                if buffer:
41	                    _execute(connection, "\n".join(buffer), output_format)
42	                return 0
43	            if line.endswith("\n"):
44	                line = line[:-1]
45	            if not buffer:
46	                text = line.strip()
47	                if not text:
48	                    continue
49	                if text.startswith("."):
50	                    parts = text.split()
51	                    if parts in ([".quit"], [".exit"]):
52	                        return 0
53	                    if parts == [".help"]:
54	                        sys.stdout.write(_HELP)
55	                    elif parts == [".tables"]:
56	                        for table in connection.tables():
57	                            sys.stdout.write(f"{table}\n")
58	                    elif parts[0] == ".schema" and len(parts) == 2:
59	                        schema = connection.schema(parts[1])
60	                        for name, kind in schema:
61	                            sys.stdout.write(f"{name} {kind}\n")
62	                    elif (parts[0] == ".format" and len(parts) == 2
63	                          and parts[1] in ("csv", "table")):
64	                        output_format = parts[1]
65	                    else:
66	                        sys.stderr.write(f"unknown command: {text}\n")
67	                    continue
68	            buffer.append(line)
69	            sql = "\n".join(buffer)
70	            if sql.rstrip().endswith(";"):
71	                _execute(connection, sql, output_format)
72	                buffer.clear()
73	        except MiniSQLError as error:
74	            _report_error(error)
75	            buffer.clear()
76	            if eof:
77	                return 0
78	
79	
80	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
81	    """Run the CLI, configuring only its output streams, never at import time."""
82	    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
83	        if hasattr(stream, "reconfigure"):
84	            stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
85	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="minisql", description="Query CSV files with SQL.")
86	    parser.add_argument("--data", default=".", metavar="DIR")
87	    parser.add_argument("--format", choices=("csv", "table"))
88	    parser.add_argument("sql", nargs="?", metavar="SQL")
89	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
90	    try:
91	        connection = connect(args.data)
92	        if args.sql is None:
93	            return _repl(connection, args.format or "table")
94	        _execute(connection, args.sql, args.format or "csv")
95	        return 0
96	    except MiniSQLError as error:
97	        _report_error(error)
98	        return 3 if isinstance(error, DataIOError) else 1
99	"

"1	# minisql
2	
3	A read-only SQL subset over a directory of CSV files. The runtime uses only the
4	Python standard library, with a handwritten lexer, AST parser, semantic analyzer
5	and executor; it does not use SQLite or another SQL engine/parser.
6	
7	## Requirements
8	
9	- Target runtime: **Python 3.11 or newer**.
10	- Run from this repository's root; no installation or runtime dependencies are
11	  required. Tests require pytest.
12	- Local validation is on macOS with the available Python 3.9.6 and pytest 8.4.2.
13	  This compatibility check does not establish supported-runtime coverage:
14	  Python 3.11+ and native Windows/Linux execution have not been verified here.
15	
16	## One-shot CLI
17	
18	Pass the entire SQL query as **one argument**:
19	
20	```sh
21	python3 -m minisql --data ./data "SELECT 1 AS one"
22	python3 -m minisql --data ./data --format table "SELECT name, salary FROM emp ORDER BY salary DESC"
23	```
24	
25	The first command writes exactly `one\n1\n`. `--data` defaults to the current
26	working directory. One-shot output defaults to CSV; `--format csv|table`
27	overrides the default. A directory must exist even for a query without `FROM`.
28	Only referenced CSV files are read, and they are reread on each query.
29	
30	Output and diagnostics use UTF-8 and LF line endings. A result is fully executed
31	and formatted before any one-shot stdout is written. Exit codes are:
32	
33	| Code | Meaning |
34	| --- | --- |
35	| 0 | Success |
36	| 1 | Lexical, parse, semantic or query-runtime error |
37	| 2 | Command-line usage error (argparse diagnostic) |
38	| 3 | Data-directory or CSV I/O error |
39	
40	Query/data errors write their formatted error line to stderr with no result on
41	stdout and no traceback. Directory validation precedes SQL lexing.
42	
43	## Interactive REPL
44	
45	Omit the SQL argument to read from stdin, interactively or through a pipe:
46	
47	```sh
48	python3 -m minisql --data ./data
49	python3 -m minisql --data ./data --format csv
50	```
51	
52	The default format is a table. Prompts are always written and flushed, including
53	when stdin is not a terminal: `minisql> ` for an empty buffer, `   ...> ` for a
54	pending query. Input is not echoed by minisql. Blank lines are ignored only when
55	the buffer is empty. Other SQL lines are joined by LF; a buffer whose
56	right-stripped text ends with `;` executes as one query and is cleared.
57	Completion is deliberately textual, not SQL-aware: semicolons inside comments
58	or unfinished string literals can trigger execution too. Errors clear the
59	buffer and the session continues, with positions relative to that buffer.
60	
61	Commands are recognized only with an empty buffer, after stripping whitespace:
62	
63	| Command | Action |
64	| --- | --- |
65	| `.help` | Show help |
66	| `.tables` | List table names in `(name.lower(), name)` order |
67	| `.schema NAME` | Print `column TYPE` for each column in header order |
68	| `.format csv` / `.format table` | Change subsequent result formatting |
69	| `.quit` / `.exit` | Exit successfully |
70	
71	Unknown commands and malformed command arguments write
72	`unknown command: <stripped command text>` to stderr and continue. At EOF a
73	pending buffer executes once, even without a semicolon; the session exits 0,
74	including after a query error. There is no farewell or extra prompt after EOF
75	is detected, but the prompt emitted before reading EOF remains in stdout.
76	
77	## Library API
78	
79	```python
80	import minisql
81	
82	connection = minisql.connect("./data")  # Validates the directory immediately.
83	print(connection.tables())
84	print(connection.schema("emp"))       # [(column_name, type_name), ...]
85	result = connection.execute("SELECT name, salary FROM emp WHERE salary > 80")
86	print(result.columns, result.types, result.rows)
87	csv_text = minisql.format_csv(result)
88	table_text = minisql.format_table(result)
89	```
90	
91	`Connection` also accepts an `os.PathLike` directory. `Result` is a frozen
92	dataclass with `columns: list[str]`, `types: list[str]`, and `rows: list[tuple]`.
93	Static types are `INTEGER`, `REAL`, `TEXT`, and `NULL`; cell values are Python
94	`int`, `float`, `str`, or `None`. Importing or using the library/formatters does
95	not reconfigure the caller's streams. Only CLI `main()` configures stdout/stderr.
96	
97	The exported errors are `MiniSQLError`, `LexError`, `ParseError`,
98	`SemanticError`, `QueryRuntimeError`, and `DataIOError`. Catch `MiniSQLError`
99	for query/data failures; `str(error)` supplies the diagnostic line. Query errors
100	expose `kind`, `message`, and 1-based `line`/`column`; data errors have no position.
101	
102	## Data, language and formats
103	
104	Each direct regular file ending in `.csv` (case-insensitive) is a table named
105	for its stem. Header names are preserved; names resolve case-insensitively.
106	CSV input is strict UTF-8 (an optional BOM is accepted). Types are inferred over
107	all nonempty column fields without trimming, and empty fields become NULL.
108	Conflicting table names, invalid headers, malformed CSV and wrong-width rows
109	produce data errors.
110	
111	The SQL subset includes expressions and aliases, `*`/`t.*`, optional `FROM`,
112	`WHERE`, inner/left joins, grouping and `HAVING`, `COUNT`/`SUM`/`AVG`/`MIN`/`MAX`,
113	`DISTINCT`, stable multi-key `ORDER BY`, and literal `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`.
114	Predicates use three-valued NULL logic; expressions are statically checked
115	before row evaluation. This is not a general-purpose SQL implementation: no
116	writes, DDL, subqueries or external SQL-engine compatibility are promised.
117	
118	CSV includes headers and no row-count footer; NULL is an unquoted empty field,
119	while empty text is quoted. Tables render NULL as `NULL`, escape embedded CR/LF,
120	and end with a row count. Both formats end every output line with LF.
121	See [contract.md](contract.md) for the complete grammar, exact formatting,
122	evaluation order and error-position rules; [brief.md](brief.md) describes the goal.
123	
124	## Tests
125	
126	From the repository root, using an environment with pytest available:
127	
128	```sh
129	python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_cli.py tests/test_repl.py
130	python3 -m pytest -q
131	python3 -m compileall -q minisql
132	```
133	
134	CLI/REPL tests assert raw subprocess bytes and exit codes with timeouts. The
135	live prompt-flush check uses POSIX subprocess pipes and is skipped on Windows;
136	other tests simulate UTF-8/LF output configuration and non-UTF-8 host encodings.
137	Simulation does not replace native cross-platform or Python 3.11+ validation.
138	"

3	A read-only SQL subset over a directory of CSV files. The runtime uses only the
4	Python standard library, with a handwritten lexer, AST parser, semantic analyzer
5	and executor; it does not use SQLite or another SQL engine/parser.
6	
7	## Requirements
8	
9	- Target runtime: **Python 3.11 or newer**.
10	- Run from this repository's root; no installation or runtime dependencies are
11	  required. Tests require pytest.
12	- Local validation is on macOS with the available Python 3.9.6 and pytest 8.4.2.
13	  This compatibility check does not establish supported-runtime coverage:
14	  Python 3.11+ and native Windows/Linux execution have not been verified here.
15	
16	## One-shot CLI
17	
18	Pass the entire SQL query as **one argument**:
19	
20	```sh
21	python3 -m minisql --data ./data "SELECT 1 AS one"
22	python3 -m minisql --data ./data --format table "SELECT name, salary FROM emp ORDER BY salary DESC"
23	```
24	
25	The first command writes exactly `one\n1\n`. `--data` defaults to the current
26	working directory. One-shot output defaults to CSV; `--format csv|table`
27	overrides the default. A directory must exist even for a query without `FROM`.
28	Only referenced CSV files are read, and they are reread on each query.
29	
30	Output and diagnostics use UTF-8 and LF line endings. A result is fully executed
31	and formatted before any one-shot stdout is written. Exit codes are:
32	
33	| Code | Meaning |
34	| --- | --- |
35	| 0 | Success |
36	| 1 | Lexical, parse, semantic or query-runtime error |
37	| 2 | Command-line usage error (argparse diagnostic) |
38	| 3 | Data-directory or CSV I/O error |
39	
40	Query/data errors write their formatted error line to stderr with no result on
41	stdout and no traceback. Directory validation precedes SQL lexing.
42	
43	## Interactive REPL
44	
45	Omit the SQL argument to read from stdin, interactively or through a pipe:
46	
47	```sh
48	python3 -m minisql --data ./data
49	python3 -m minisql --data ./data --format csv
50	```
51	
52	The default format is a table. Prompts are always written and flushed, including
53	when stdin is not a terminal: `minisql> ` for an empty buffer, `   ...> ` for a
54	pending query. Input is not echoed by minisql. Blank lines are ignored only when
55	the buffer is empty. Other SQL lines are joined by LF; a buffer whose
56	right-stripped text ends with `;` executes as one query and is cleared.
57	Completion is deliberately textual, not SQL-aware: semicolons inside comments
58	or unfinished string literals can trigger execution too. Errors clear the
59	buffer and the session continues, with positions relative to that buffer.
60	
61	Commands are recognized only with an empty buffer, after stripping whitespace:
62	
63	| Command | Action |
64	| --- | --- |
65	| `.help` | Show help |
66	| `.tables` | List table names in `(name.lower(), name)` order |
67	| `.schema NAME` | Print `column TYPE` for each column in header order |
68	| `.format csv` / `.format table` | Change subsequent result formatting |
69	| `.quit` / `.exit` | Exit successfully |
70	
71	Unknown commands and malformed command arguments write
72	`unknown command: <stripped command text>` to stderr and continue. At EOF a
73	pending buffer executes once, even without a semicolon; the session exits 0,
74	including after a query error. There is no farewell or extra prompt after EOF
75	is detected, but the prompt emitted before reading EOF remains in stdout.
76	
77	## Library API
78	
79	```python
80	import minisql
81	
82	connection = minisql.connect("./data")  # Validates the directory immediately.
83	print(connection.tables())
84	print(connection.schema("emp"))       # [(column_name, type_name), ...]
85	result = connection.execute("SELECT name, salary FROM emp WHERE salary > 80")
86	print(result.columns, result.types, result.rows)
87	csv_text = minisql.format_csv(result)
88	table_text = minisql.format_table(result)
89	```
90	
91	`Connection` also accepts an `os.PathLike` directory. `Result` is a frozen
92	dataclass with `columns: list[str]`, `types: list[str]`, and `rows: list[tuple]`.
93	Static types are `INTEGER`, `REAL`, `TEXT`, and `NULL`; cell values are Python
94	`int`, `float`, `str`, or `None`. Importing or using the library/formatters does
95	not reconfigure the caller's streams. Only CLI `main()` configures stdout/stderr.
96	
97	The exported errors are `MiniSQLError`, `LexError`, `ParseError`,
98	`SemanticError`, `QueryRuntimeError`, and `DataIOError`. Catch `MiniSQLError`
99	for query/data failures; `str(error)` supplies the diagnostic line. Query errors
100	expose `kind`, `message`, and 1-based `line`/`column`; data errors have no position.
101	
102	## Data, language and formats
103	
104	Each direct regular file ending in `.csv` (case-insensitive) is a table named
105	for its stem. Header names are preserved; names resolve case-insensitively.
106	CSV input is strict UTF-8 (an optional BOM is accepted). Types are inferred over
107	all nonempty column fields without trimming, and empty fields become NULL.
108	Conflicting table names, invalid headers, malformed CSV and wrong-width rows
109	produce data errors.
110	
111	The SQL subset includes expressions and aliases, `*`/`t.*`, optional `FROM`,
112	`WHERE`, inner/left joins, grouping and `HAVING`, `COUNT`/`SUM`/`AVG`/`MIN`/`MAX`,
113	`DISTINCT`, stable multi-key `ORDER BY`, and literal `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`.
114	Predicates use three-valued NULL logic; expressions are statically checked
115	before row evaluation. This is not a general-purpose SQL implementation: no
116	writes, DDL, subqueries or external SQL-engine compatibility are promised.
117	
118	CSV includes headers and no row-count footer; NULL is an unquoted empty field,
119	while empty text is quoted. Tables render NULL as `NULL`, escape embedded CR/LF,
120	and end with a row count. Both formats end every output line with LF.
121	See [contract.md](contract.md) for the complete grammar, exact formatting,
122	evaluation order and error-position rules; [brief.md](brief.md) describes the goal.

12	import pkgutil
13	import sys
14	import sysconfig
15

18	
19	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

40	def import_targets(tree):
41	    """Yield static imports, including literal dynamic-import calls.
42	
43	    Unresolvable dynamic imports fail the audit rather than silently passing.
44	    Relative imports are checked against the on-disk package separately.
45	    """
46	    for node in ast.walk(tree):
47	        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
48	            for alias in node.names:

50	        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
51	            yield node.module or "", node.level, node.lineno
52	        elif isinstance(node, ast.Call):
53	            function = node.func
54	            dynamic = (isinstance(function, ast.Name) and function.id == "__import__") or (
55	                isinstance(function, ast.Attribute) and function.attr == "import_module")

46	        nonlocal i, line, column
47	        text = sql[i:end]
48	        newlines = text.count("\n")

71	            while end < len(sql):

40	    keyword values are uppercase and EOF's value is None.
41	    """
42	    tokens = []
43	    i, line, column = 0, 1, 1

45	    def advance(end: int) -> None:
46	        nonlocal i, line, column
47	        text = sql[i:end]
48	        newlines = text.count("\n")
49	        if newlines:

51	            column = len(text.rsplit("\n", 1)[1]) + 1

18

20	|---|---|
21	| kind | `INT`, `REAL`, `STRING`, `IDENT`, `QUOTED_IDENT`, `EOF`, an uppercase keyword, or the operator/punctuation itself |

"1	# minisql: Brief
2	
3	Build `minisql`, a query engine for a read-only SQL subset over a directory of CSV files, in Python 3.11+ using only the standard library. Each CSV file is a table; columns get an inferred type of INTEGER, REAL or TEXT, and empty fields are NULL. Support SELECT with expressions and aliases, WHERE with full NULL three-valued logic, LIKE and IN, INNER and LEFT JOIN, GROUP BY with HAVING and the five standard aggregates, DISTINCT, multi-key ORDER BY, and LIMIT/OFFSET. Structure it as a real engine: tokenizer, parser producing an AST, semantic analysis, and an executor. Expose a library API, a one-shot CLI that prints CSV or an aligned table, and an interactive REPL. Errors must be one line naming their kind and the exact query line and column, never a traceback. Do not use `sqlite3` or any existing SQL engine or parser. Output must be byte-for-byte deterministic on Windows, macOS and Linux. The full contract is in `contract.md`; include pytest tests for your implementation.
4	"

13	## Lexer protocol
14	
15	`from minisql.lexer import Token, tokenize`; `tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]` lexes the whole string, including a terminal EOF token. `KEYWORDS` is the exact reserved set, a frozenset of uppercase strings; aggregate function names remain ordinary identifiers.
16	
17	`Token` is a frozen dataclass with fields, in order:
18	
19	| Field | Meaning |
20	|---|---|
21	| kind | `INT`, `REAL`, `STRING`, `IDENT`, `QUOTED_IDENT`, `EOF`, an uppercase keyword, or the operator/punctuation itself |
22	| raw | Exact token source spelling, including any quotes |
23	| value | int/float for numbers; decoded str for names/strings; uppercase str for keywords; raw symbol for punctuation; None for EOF |
24	| start, end | Zero-based code-point offsets, end-exclusive |
25	| line, column | One-based token-start coordinates; only LF splits lines |
26	
27	In particular, a NULL token is a keyword token whose value is `"NULL"`; consumers derive the NULL literal's type/value from its kind, not from token.value. `007` decodes to int 7, `1e2` to float 100.0. Quoted names retain their case in decoded value; resolution later uses lower(), not casefold(). Unicode is accepted inside quotes, not in unquoted ASCII identifiers or numbers. Numeric continuation checking is ASCII as specified in feature-specification.md §5.2. Comments end only at LF. EOF has raw `""`, value None, start=end=len(sql), and the position immediately after all input, including trailing whitespace/comments.
28	
29	## Parser entry and ownership boundary
30	
31	`from minisql.parser import parse`; `parse(sql: str) -> minisql.ast.Query` fully tokenizes before constructing the parser, so LexError anywhere in the input precedes a possible ParseError. No catalog, name/function resolution, static typing, execution, or output formatting occurs here. For example, unknown function names, non-COUNT star calls, and multi-character literal ESCAPEs parse and await semantic validation.
32	
33	All AST records are frozen dataclasses, with inherited `start: int, end: int` fields first. Spans are code-point offsets into `Query.source`, end-exclusive. All sequence fields below are tuples. Optional tokens/nodes use None. All name/alias/operator/star/ESCAPE fields below are original lexer Token objects, not rewritten strings.
34	
35	### Expressions (`minisql.ast.Expr` subclasses)
36	
37	- `Literal(start, end, token)`: INT/REAL/STRING/NULL; token.kind preserves static literal kind and token.value preserves decoded numeric/string values.
38	- `Column(start, end, name, qualifier)`: name Token and optional qualifier Token. A qualified reference starts at its qualifier. Both IDENT and QUOTED_IDENT are accepted.
39	- `Unary(start, end, operator, operand)`: unary +/- or prefix NOT. The operator is its exact token.
40	- `Binary(start, end, left, operator, right)`: arithmetic, comparisons, AND, OR. Keyword operator kinds are uppercase, raw spelling remains unchanged; != and <> remain distinct.
41	- `IsNull(start, end, operand, operator, not_token, null_token)`: operator is IS, optional not_token is NOT.
42	- `Like(start, end, operand, operator, pattern, not_token, escape_keyword, escape)`: operator is LIKE even for NOT LIKE; escape_keyword is ESCAPE and escape is its STRING token. Runtime LIKE errors belong at operator; invalid ESCAPE length belongs at escape.
43	- `In(start, end, operand, operator, items, not_token, lparen, rparen)`: operator is IN even for NOT IN; items is a nonempty tuple of full expressions.
44	- `Call(start, end, name, argument, star, lparen, rparen)`: exactly one of argument Expr or star Token is present. Name is an ordinary or quoted name token. COUNT(*)'s star position is available directly.
45	- `Parenthesized(start, end, expression, lparen, rparen)`: explicit wrapper, including nested wrappers, with its own outer span. Parentheses are not erased during parsing.
46	
47	Precedence is unary signs > multiplicative > additive > one comparison/predicate > recursive NOT > left-associative AND > left-associative OR. Comparisons cannot chain without explicit parentheses; failure is at the second operator. Calls take one expression or star; IN has at least one expression. LIMIT/OFFSET take INT tokens, never signed, real, or parenthesized expressions.
48	
49	### Query and surrounding records
50	
51	- `Wildcard(start, end, star, qualifier)`: a Node, not an Expr; star Token and optional qualifier Token for bare * or q.*. Only projection items accept it.
52	- `SelectItem(start, end, expression, alias, as_token)`: expression is Expr or Wildcard; alias and as_token are optional name/AS tokens. Explicit AS and implicit aliases remain distinguishable. A SelectItem span includes its alias when present, while its expression span never includes that alias. Wildcards have no alias production.
53	- `TableRef(start, end, name, alias, as_token)`: name/alias Tokens; effective range name is alias if present, else name. TableRef span includes its alias.
54	- `Join(start, end, kind, table, condition, keyword, join_token, outer_token, on_token)`: kind is `INNER` for JOIN/INNER JOIN, `LEFT` for LEFT [OUTER] JOIN. keyword is the first JOIN/INNER/LEFT token; join_token is JOIN; outer_token exists only for LEFT OUTER JOIN; on_token is ON. condition is a complete Expr.
55	- `OrderItem(start, end, expression, direction)`: optional ASC/DESC Token; None means ASC. Span includes a direction if present; expression span does not.
56	- `Query(start, end, source, select_token, distinct, items, from_table, joins, where, group_by, having, order_by, limit, offset, semicolon)`: source is the entire original sql string. distinct is its DISTINCT Token or None. items is a nonempty SelectItem tuple. from_table is optional; joins are in source order. where/having are optional expressions. group_by and order_by are tuples, empty when absent. limit/offset are optional unsigned INT Tokens; use `.value` for the integer. semicolon is its optional token. Query span runs from SELECT through the last syntactic token, including a semicolon when present but excluding trailing comments/whitespace. EOF consumes all remaining input; only one semicolon is accepted.

For resolved structural identity, unwrap Parenthesized recursively; ignore spans/token spelling; preserve literal kind plus decoded value, operator kind/symbol identity, operand order, and resolved column identities.
